Sources indicate that bob Seger and the Silver Bullet Band bassist Chris Campbell, who joined forces with Seger in 1969 and remained a core member of the band through Seger’s farewell tour in 2019 — playing on timeless hits like “Turn the Page,” “Night Moves,” “Rock and Roll Never Forgets,” “Still the Same,” “Hollywood Nights,” and “Against the Wind” — died on Sunday. He was 78.

Campbell’s wife, Courtney, confirmed his death with Rolling Stone, adding that Campbell died of natural causes.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m grieving the loss of my long-time friend and Silver Bullet bandmate, Chris Campbell…..RIP,” Silver Bullet Band vocalist Shaun Murphy wrote. “Prayers and condolences to his wonderful wife, Courtney Campbell, and his three beautiful daughters!! I am forever grateful for all the cherished memories I have.”.

In a recent development, campbell grew up in Plymouth, Michigan, and was a regular on the Detroit club scene that gave rise to the MC5, the Stooges, and the Amboy Dukes. “You were playing to smaller crowds and things were more intimate,” he told the Observer & Eccentric in 1987. “There weren’t any barriers in front of the stage with six-foot security guards.”.

Just one year after the Bob Seger System scored a nationwide hit with “Ramblin’ Gamblin’ Man” in 1968, Campbell was offered a spot in the band. “I was hired in what I thought was a temporary job as bass player because Dan Honaker had just broken his wrist about a week before the Mongrel tour [in a motorcycle accident],” he told Rolling Stone in 2011. “I had a week to prepare. I had to learn this album frontwards and backwards.”.

Honaker’s bad luck turned out to be the opportunity of a lifetime for Campbell because of what transpired not long after the Bob Seger System dissolved. “Bob called me…I think it was ’71, ’72,” Campbell told Rolling Stone. “He mentioned, ‘I’m thinking of putting a band together.’ I said to him, ‘That’s kind of bizarre, I have a keyboard player and a drummer.’ He goes, ‘I got a guitarist, Drew Abbott.’ That was the start of the Silver Bullet Band.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

The early years of the Silver Bullet Band were a brutal grind, memorialized in the lyrics of 1972’s “Turn the Page,” but everything changed once the concert LP Live Bullet took off in 1976. The follow-up LP, Night Moves, turned Seger into one of the biggest names in rock.

Unlike similar groups like Bruce Springsteen’s E Street Band and Neil Young’s Crazy Horse, membership in the Silver Bullet Band was somewhat fluid, and studio musicians often backed Seger on albums. This arrangement didn’t suit Abbott, who quit the group in 1983 and never returned. But Campbell, background singers Shaun Murphy and Laura Creamer, and saxophonist Alto Reed were lifers. Grand Funk Railroad keyboardist Craig Frost also became a key component of the group for decades.

In a recent development, for Campbell, it wasn’t always an easy ride. “We have all [thought about leaving] at one time or another,” he told the Observer & Eccentric in 1987. “It would be an out-and-out lie to say we haven’t. You get tired, and it’s terrible on relationships.”.

The job got easier after the tour for Seger’s 1995 LP It’s a Mystery wrapped, and the group went off the road for more than a decade. “Bob works at his own pace,” Campbell told Rolling Stone in 2011. “I can go out and do something else. It’s the way it’s always been since 1969. I wouldn’t know any other way. This is my life, and I’m very happy with it. I have wonderful kids and a good life, and we’re all friends. We’re all very fortunate. There’s no animosity and no fighting. Bob is our rock, our patriarch. We all look up to him. He’s so easy to work with. He’s a wonderful man, just as a human being.” Related Content John Christ, Original Danzig Guitarist on ‘Mother’ and More, Dead at 61 Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys’ Bass Singer, Dead at 83 Anthony Clark, Stand-Up Comic and 'Yes, Dear' Star, Dead at 62 Stacy Keach, ‘Mike Hammer’ and ‘Fat City’ Star, Dead at 85.

Sources indicate that bob Seger and the Silver Bullet Band rolled out a farewell tour in 2018 that wrapped up in 2019 at the Wells Fargo Center in Philadelphia. They became just about the only act in rock history to say farewell and truly mean it. Industry observers note that two years after the tour wrapped, Campbell filed a lawsuit against Seger and longtime manager Punch Andrews over alleged unpaid royalties from albums and tours. “Bob Seger and Punch Andrews have loyally supported our friend for 45-plus years,” they said in a statement. (Campbell ultimately lost his recording-royalty claims.).

It has been revealed that campbell kept a low public profile after the farewell tour. But in 2011, he told Rolling Stone why he enjoyed the latter-day tours so much. “We’re kind of old-school,” he said. “We aren’t glitzy. You don’t see any flash pots going off up there. We just do things the way we do. We aren’t really concerned about press agents and all that. We just play. And the older we get, the more fun we have. When you get older, you don’t take it as seriously as you once did when you were younger. If you can’t have fun at our age, don’t do it.”.

Canva introduces new controls to hide generative AI features

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In light of growing pushback from owners who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing upcoming settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content.
  • Canva today declared latest controls that will let Free and Pro owners choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.
  • The company notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In light of growing pushback from owners who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing upcoming settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content. Here are the details.

Canva today declared latest controls that will let Free and Pro owners choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

The company notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.

According to Canva, “the future of creativity isn’t a choice between AI and no AI.” For this reason, it is introducing the following controls:.

The company claims that, while it knows that there is an ongoing debate between consumers with opposing views on whether AI has a place in creative work, it thinks “both views are valid”:.

“It’s not our place to tell anyone how to create, so today we’re launching two new controls that put that decision firmly with our community […].”.

Importantly, the firm noted that select features that use AI without generating latest content will remain available even when generative AI features are turned off:.

“Some of Canva’s everyday editing tools use AI to make simple tasks faster, without generating anything fresh. Background Remover, one of Canva’s most popular tools, lifts a subject cleanly out of a photo in a single click, and Magic Grab lets creators select an object in an image and move it somewhere else in the design. Both remain available when the generative AI switch is off, because they work only with what’s already in a design.”.

Canva added that these tools also won’t add an AI label to a design’s metadata, since that label is reserved for AI-generated content.

As for the company’s design content library, Canva remarked that while “a small portion of the library is AI-generated content made by Canva, including some abstract backgrounds and illustrated graphics,” its community has told it “they want an easier way to find design assets made by real people, so the content control reduces the number of AI-generated templates and elements that appear in search results and recommendations.”.

With today’s announcement, Canva is essentially expanding on the AI permissions already available to administrators of Business, Enterprise, Teams, and Education accounts, which let organizations control how their teams use AI.

In a recent development, ms. Rachel met with children appearing without an attorney at federal youth immigration court in Manhattan on Monday. The children’s educator and YouTuber highlighted the lack of legal representation for children facing deportation and their families as they struggle to navigate the complex immigration system in the United States.

Ms. Rachel, a vocal critic of the Trump administration’s family detainment practices and harmful rhetoric against immigrant children, shared a video on social media of nine-year-old Angel, who appeared in court without an attorney amid immigration proceedings.

“Kids representing themselves in immigration court is so wrong. I saw Angel up at the mic without a lawyer and I couldn’t believe it. He’s 9 years old!” Ms. Rachel wrote in the caption. “Hearing kids hear the word ‘removable’ over and over about themselves… Heartbreaking. Stop the cruelty!”.

Sources indicate that when Ms. Rachel asked Angel to write a list of things he wanted for Christmas, he asked for an immigration lawyer. “I am getting Angel a lawyer,” wrote the educator.

Ms. Rachel stopped by the court alongside Congressman-elect Brad Lander, according to ABC 7. The outlet remarked that a judge gave Angel’s mother until Dec. 15 to obtain legal representation.“It’s heartbreaking. I care so much about every child and I just want to see every child thriving in school and my heart goes out to anyone going through this,” Ms. Rachel said, per the outlet. “I think about how that makes a child feel whether or not you are removable…I don’t want any child to hear that word associated with them.”.

The YouTube personality called attention to policymakers and stated they needed to better prioritize the needs of children. “I think our problems would really be a lot less if we all just focus on taking care of kids and centered kids in policies,” she said. #165661. 10 'Find Hub' Hacks Every Android User Should Know

📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

10 'Find Hub' Hacks Every Android User Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1298 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone.
  • This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually.
  • It has been revealed that there’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google's Find Hub app isn't just for tracking your lost smartphone. Over the past year, Google has consistently added features to manage your belongings, share your location with loved ones, and locate lost devices. Find Hub can now notify you when you've left your device or your tracker behind. Plus, you can use Gemini to remember where you left items, even without a tracker attached. Behind the scenes, there are even more hidden settings and features to help track your devices and make it easier to retrieve them in case they are stolen or misplaced. If you use Find Hub, you need to know about these 10 hacks.

This month, Google finally added Left Behind notifications to Android trackers—but you have to enable the feature manually. AirTags users should be familiar with this feature already. When you leave your tracker or device behind, and exit the location range, you’ll receive a notification that you left without your item. You need to enable this feature on a per-device basis. Go to Find Hub and select a device. Tap the settings gear icon next to the device's name, and enable Notify when left behind. While you’re here, go to Add location to add familiar locations where you don’t want to get a notification (like your home or workspace). Otherwise, Find Hub may spam you with left behind alerts.

It has been revealed that there’s a hidden feature in the Find Hub app that helps you keep track of things without actually using a Bluetooth tracker. You can simply ask Gemini to remember where you put things, and it will show up in the Find Hub app. To use it, pull up Gemini and say something like, “Remember in Find Hub that the passport is in the downstairs wardrobe,” or “I’ve kept the spare car keys behind the garage door.”.

You can then ask Gemini, “Where did I keep my passport?” and it will tell you. If you change the location of an item, just ask Gemini to enhancement it for you. When you go to the Remembered tab, you’ll see the location of all remembered items. You can also add items manually here using the Add button.

It has been revealed that some Android smartphones can remain findable for several hours after they've been switched off or their batteries have run out. If you’re using a supported device (like the latest Pixel series smartphone), you can use a hardware feature to track the location using Google’s mesh network, relying on nearby devices (similar to how Android tags work).

According to recent reports, to make sure this feature is enabled, go to Find Hub, and tap Find your offline devices. Here, make sure that either With network in busy places only or With network everywhere is selected.

If you’re using a tracker in your car, luggage, or on your keys, you might want to share location access with your spouse or family members. Find Hub has a feature called "Share Ownership" that lets you share the tracker details with up to 10 people. Only the location of your tracker is shared, not your personal device.

It has been revealed that to set it up, go to Find Hub, and choose the tracker or accessory that you want to share. Tap the Share Ownership button and follow the on-screen instructions to share the invite link via a messaging app or using Quick Share. Once the recipient taps Accept, you’ll get a notification. Go to the device settings in Find Hub and tap the Confirm button to enable location sharing.

You can swiftly share your live location with your friends or loved ones using Google Messages. Open a conversation, tap the Attachment icon, and choose Real-time location. Set the duration and tap Send.

If you don’t like using the Messages app, you can do so directly from Find Hub. Go to the People tab at the bottom of the screen, and tap the Plus icon. Choose the duration and select a contact to share the location with, then tap the Get Link button to copy the link. You can then share it via any messaging app of your choice.

In a recent development, you might have a Find Hub tracker in your luggage to help keep tabs on your bags. But you don't have to be the only one privy to its location. If your airline loses that luggage, you can temporarily share its location with your airline to help you retrieve it. This is an official feature, too: Google partnered with multiple airlines to make this data sharing easier. From the Find Hub, choose your tracker. Tap the Share Item Location button, and then tap Share Item Location again. Copy the generated web link and share it with your airline using the app or support page. The link will automatically expire in seven days, so you don't have to worry about your airline continuing to monitor your luggage's location long after your flight.

Find Hub uses a mesh network of supported Android devices to securely locate your lost device or tag. But by default, it waits until multiple Android devices detect the location of the lost device. This works well if you've lost the device in crowded areas, but it can increase your wait time if you lose it somewhere remote. Luckily, there is a hidden setting that triggers location sharing even if a single device reports its location. Go to Settings > Google > All services > Find Hub > Find your offline devices and select With network everywhere instead of With network in busy places only.

It has been revealed that if you’ve lost your smartphone, you don’t need to rush to a computer or a website to track it. Borrow someone’s Android smartphone and head into their Find Hub. Tap Sign in as guest and sign in with your Google account associated with your device, then find and select your device in the account. If requested, enter the PIN that you’ve previously set up. You can now track the device’s location, get directions to the device, or play a sound to help track the device if it’s nearby. If the device is truly lost, you can use the Mark as Lost feature to remotely lock your device.

It has been revealed that map-based tracking is helpful in getting to the general vicinity of your lost device. But your smartphone or tracker is hidden; finding it may require precision tracking. Many newer trackers like the Pixel Tag come with an ultra-wideband chip that helps you find the exact location of the tracker, given you are nearby. This also works on Pixel smartphones (Pixel 8 Pro series and above) and Samsung Galaxy devices (S21 and above, Plus and Ultra models only).

According to recent reports, when using this feature, make sure you have Bluetooth enabled on your smartphone, then open Find Hub. Choose your tracker, and tap Find Nearby. Follow the on-screen instructions to locate the nearby device. You can also tap Play Sound to make the location process easier.

If you think your Android smartphone is lost or stolen, don’t rush to erase all data. While a remote factory reset is great for protecting your data, it also removes the device from your account. It’s best to try to get the device back. Two-factor authentication (or a passkey) on your Google account, along with a biometric lock on your smartphone, will protect the data itself.

Go to the Find Hub website, or use Find Hub on someone else’s phone in guest mode. Choose your device, and instead of Factory Reset, choose Mark as Lost. Here, you’ll see an option to enter a message. Type an alternative contact number, and a message to help recover the device.

  • The company is mentioned to be holding discussions with display partner Samsung about either delaying the planned launch or abandoning it altogether, with two reasons cited ….
  • 24” is undesirable at the prices they ask.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is considering abandoning aims to launch an OLED iMac, according to a new supply chain report. The news comes just weeks after the first OLED Mac was launched in the form of the new touchscreen MacBook Pro.

The company is mentioned to be holding discussions with display partner Samsung about either delaying the planned launch or abandoning it altogether, with two reasons cited ….

1. The size. 24” is undesirable at the prices they ask.

2. No target display mode. Making the display unusable with multiple computers or after you’ve upgraded to a newly introduced model of Mac.

Adding OLED doesn’t solve either of these, and raising the price obviously doesn’t solve it.

Industry observers note that at the same time, there’s an crucial distinction between commercial viability and margins. Apple is concerned with the latter, not the former.

It has been revealed that an OLED iMac would be a commercially viable product at current prices, but it might not have the 30 to 40 % hardware profit margins they desire. Adding OLED would raise Apples costs, without adding more sales (due to 1 and 2) to offset that slightly lower but (still industry leading) profit margin.

Apple’s journey into OLED screens began with the Apple Watch while other products were still using IPS LCD. The firm subsequently switched to OLED for some iPhones and iPads before a long-awaited launch of the first OLED MacBook Pro back in October.

It was expected that the company would gradually transition to OLED across the full range of Macs over time. However, this process was expected to take a number of years, with the iMac not likely to join the party until 2029 or 2030.

The Elec today reports that the move may be delayed even further or even abandoned altogether, for two reasons: cost and demand.

The company is mentioned to be discussing a potential delay or cancellation of the project with Samsung Display. High OLED panel costs and weak sales of existing OLED-equipped products are believed to be factors behind the reconsideration […].

The biggest factor behind the review is cost. The iMac sells in smaller volumes than smartphones or laptops, making it difficult to maintain competitive pricing if expensive OLED panels are adopted. Weak sales of the OLED iPad Pro are also believed to have influenced the decision.

In a recent development, the report suggests that incoming CEO John Ternus has been reviewing the commercial viability of upgrading more products to OLED. As further evidence, the report says Apple has sent quotation requests to LCD suppliers for an iMac screen to be introduced in around 2029.

From nostalgic knockouts to broomstick-flying drama, here’s a guide to everything new on HBO Max in December 2026.

In a recent development, one of the most talked-about latest movies of the so-called "awards season" thus far has been "I Play Rocky," an underdog biopic starring Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone during the tumultuous production of his iconic boxing flick "Rocky," which famously went on to win the Oscar for Best Picture. But before you tune into that new bio-drama, why not go back to where it all started with a big "Rocky" movie marathon?

Industry observers note that helpfully, HBO Max isn't just bringing back the 1976 original — which is celebrating its significant 50th anniversary this year and centers on a small-time Philadelphia boxer (Stallone) who gets a once-in-a-lifetime chance to face the world heavyweight champion in the ring — but all nine films in the "Rocky" franchise beginning on December 1. Jordan-led "Creed" spinoff trilogy comprising “Creed” (2015), “Creed II” (2018) and “Creed III” (2023).

That should keep you busy until New Year's, right?

Stream "I Want Your Sex" on HBO Max starting December 4.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I've read more than 30 books in the past year, all of them on an e-reader with a screen roughly the size of a credit card. If you think that sounds untenable, I say: Don't knock it 'til you've tried it. Once you're immersed in a book, you'll find the size doesn't matter, and the convenience of being able to slip it into any pocket and forget it's there means you need never be without it.

Right now, the Xteink X4 Pro, the best tiny e-reader I've tried so far—and Lifehacker's pick for the 2026 E-Reader Gift of the Year—is on its best sale yet for Black Friday: When ordered directly from Xteink, you'll save 15% off the usual $99 price, bringing it down to $84. This is the cheapest e-reader with a light and a touchscreen that you can buy right now, and it's well worth the money.

The X4 Pro is the newest and best e-reader from Xteink, the Chinese tech startup that turned the e-reading world upside down last year with the launch of the original X4 pocket e-reader. While the X4 Pro is the same size as the basic X4 Classic, it adds two significant upgrades—a temperature-adjustable front light and a touchscreen—plus a faster processor and more memory. As a result, it costs a bit more, but you can pick one at a $15 discount right now. (Even at full retail, the X4 Pro is $50 cheaper than the entry-level Kindle after its recent price increase—and even considering the Kindle's current Black Friday discount).

Meanwhile, if you're a reader who prioritizes the crispest text over conveniences like a front light, the 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic and the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 are about $30 less during Amazon's own Black Friday sale.

As much as I love them, these minuscule e-readers aren't for everyone. Some may indeed find the screen too small (though if you've ever read a book on a phone, the experience is similar). Then there's the fact that they can't load your existing libraries of Kindle books; you'll need to source copies of e-books lacking Digital Rights Management (DRM) software. But if you can jump those hurdles, you might just discover it's the weirdest, most lovable piece of tech you've used in years.

According to recent reports, while she was fairly vague about the kinds of companies she has been talking to, Bajaria indicated the conversations were active. “Everything is about how to connect to the audience,” she remarked. “And I have always been passionate about them. And that reveals up in lots of different ways.”.

Sources indicate that onstage, Bajaria obliquely referenced her abrupt exit from Netflix in her acceptance speech. “Around the world, this is a season of holidays – some we’ve just celebrated, others still ahead,” she said. “For some of us, it’s a season of change, as you might have heard. But more than anything, for me, it’s a season of gratitude.”.

Keri Russell, star of Netflix drama The Diplomat, presented Bajaria with the award at the Latest York Hilton in Midtown Manhattan. The exec referenced Russell after being handed the Emmy statuette, and it was hard not to try to read into her comments as she reflected on the topic of leadership.

“Keri and I have talked a lot about leadership,” Bajaria remarked. “And I agree with her, that a leader must take care of the group. In our business, but really in any business, leadership matters. Bajaria concluded her remarks with a little teaser. “As for me, I’ve never been more excited for the next season,” she mentioned. “You know I love to surprise an audience. So stay tuned.”.

In the Deadline interview, the exec stated she has “gotten a lot of advice” in recent weeks, much of which implored her to “explore, be open. Don’t make any decisions.” Bearing that in mind, she continued, “Looking at my career in TV also evolved, and had a lot of building of and innovations. And so, for me, that idea of building and invention is super important.”.

International Emmy organizers earlier had remarked Bajaria was receiving the honor “in recognition of her transformational leadership.” Prior to her 10-year run at Netflix, including six years as chief content officer, she was president of Universal Television and held senior posts at CBS Television Studios and CBS Network.

Along with The Diplomat, Bajaria helped shepherd global hits like Stranger Things, Bridgerton and Squid Game and also steered Netflix through its ramp-up of unscripted programming and entry into live sports.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Magnesium is one of the most popular supplements on the market thanks to wide-ranging potential benefits like better sleep, stress reduction, and improved digestion. Much of this popularity has been driven by social media, including the viral #SleepyGirlMocktail trend. Plus, a slew of A-listers from Taylor Swift to Scarlett Johansson to Lenny Kravitz have also talked about taking magnesium to relax.

So what is magnesium? Like most supplements, it’s a mineral used by our body’s cells to function. It helps turn food into energy, strengthen bones, and support normal heart rhythm. Another key function of magnesium is sleep regulation, since the mineral helps calm muscles and the nervous system and regulate sleep-related hormones. That means taking magnesium may help consumers get better natural sleep instead of being sedated.

There are several types of magnesium supplements, and each binds magnesium to a different molecule, affecting absorption and how the supplement is used. “Magnesium citrate, chloride, lactate, and aspartate generally have better bioavailability than magnesium oxide because they are more soluble and more readily absorbed,” Dr. Martina Ambardjieva, MD, Ph.D., urologist, and medical expert at Invigor Medical, tells Rolling Stone. “Magnesium glycinate also tends to be well tolerated.”.

Studies show that magnesium citrate may support digestion and bowel regularity, chloride muscle and nerve function, lactate energy production, aspartate muscle function and energy, and glycinate relaxation, sleep, and stress management. According to Ambardjieva, the recommended total daily magnesium intake is approximately 310 to 320 milligrams daily for women and 400 to 420 milligrams for men, including food sources.

In a recent development, in order to choose the right magnesium supplement for your health and lifestyle, Ambardjieva recommends checking the amount of elemental magnesium (the actual weight of the magnesium in the supplement) and avoiding unnecessarily high doses. The best magnesium supplements also have third-party testing, such as USP or NSF verification.

If you’re looking to try magnesium for yourself, pick up one of the supplements below.

Pros: High dose, can be mixed with waterCons: May cause bathroom urges.

Thorne Magnesium Citrate delivers 250 mg of highly absorbable magnesium in a convenient citrus-berry powder that can be mixed with water, ideal for those who don’t feel comfortable swallowing pills. Although a powder, it’s not recommended to take it before bed, like other powders in the #SleepyGirlMocktail trend, as magnesium citrate is a type of laxative. On the other hand, it supports muscle and cardiovascular health, promotes regular digestion, and helps maintain urinary mineral balance, with NSF certification.

Pros: Approved by over 32,000 Amazon customersCons: Reviewers say there is an aftertaste.

It has been revealed that bioEmblem’s Triple Complex provides 300 mg per serving from glycinate, malate, and citrate. The three types of magnesium here promote bone health and muscle support, and the brand is third-party tested and NSF- and Labdoor-certified. However, it does not clearly distinguish how much of the 300 mg is elemental magnesium. Still, it’s proven to be a popular option among customers, with over 32,000 reviews and a 4.6-star rating on Amazon.

Pros: Dual-amino-acid chelate formula for better absorption, powder form, great for relaxationCons: Flavor might not be for everyone.

Unlike the other options on this list, this one from Viactiv uses magnesium lysinate glycinate, a dual-amino-acid chelate. In plain English, this is meant to improve absorption and digestive tolerability of the magnesium, which is a common side effect that people report. It’s a powder, which is great for mixing with water or shakes, and comes in a stevia-sweetened peach flavor.

Pros: Supports bone, heart, nerve, and immune health in oneCons: The dose is higher than what is doctor-recommended for adults.

In a recent development, vitalitown’s Magnesium Complex provides four forms: glycinate, citrate, taurate, and malate. The product is NSF certified and third-party tested. At 500 mg per serving, its dose is relatively high compared with typical daily magnesium needs, making dose awareness important. As Dr. Ambardjieva tells us, there isn’t one ideal supplemental dose for everyone, so guidance from your physician about the right dose is recommended.

Pros: Targets fatigue, muscle issues, and constipationCons: Lower mgs than what is doctor-recommended for an adult to take daily.

Sources indicate that double Wood’s Magnesium Chloride provides 120 mg of elemental magnesium per serving and includes chloride, which Ambardjieva identified as generally well absorbed. In addition to promoting sleep and supporting muscle and nerve function, studies show that magnesium chloride is a good option for when your body is already deficient. According to the doctor, magnesium deficiency may cause fatigue, weakness, nausea, muscle cramps, tingling, and, in severe cases, seizures or irregular heart rhythms. Double Wood Supplements is also described as third-party tested for purity, potency, microbes, and heavy metals.

Pros: Gentle on the stomachCons: Must take three large capsules to reach the recommended dose for an adult.

According to recent reports, nature Made Magnesium Glycinate provides 300 mg per three capsules and clearly identifies the amount of magnesium provided. Although Ambardjieva notes there is less comparative evidence showing that magnesium glycinate is clearly superior to other well-absorbed forms, research indicates that magnesium glycinate is a stomach-friendly supplement, unlike magnesium oxide, and may reduce stress and muscle tension, among other benefits. The product is also USP verified, addressing the recommendation to look for independent quality testing.

Pros: Lactose-free and absorbs quickly into the bloodstream Cons: Customers say the pill size is quite large compared to other magnesium capsules.

In a recent development, swanson Magnesium Lactate provides 84 mg of elemental magnesium per capsule and is among the forms Ambardjieva identified as generally well absorbed due to its high bioavailability. Research suggests that magnesium lactate causes fewer digestive side effects than some other forms of magnesium, and may support healthy blood pressure and normal cell function. Swanson also says its finished supplements undergo independent third-party laboratory testing for purity and potency.

Pros: Vegan ingredients and the best magnesium supplement for athletesCons: The glass jar makes it susceptible to breaking, according to some reviewers.

Bluebonnet Magnesium Aspartate provides 400 mg daily as magnesium aspartate, a form Ambardjieva identified as generally well absorbed. The brand’s supplements undergo rigorous testing for authenticity, purity, and potency, although it does not specifically mention USP or NSF verification. Scientists found that magnesium aspartate helps with proper muscle contraction and is a popular magnesium form for athletes.

Pros: A vegan and kosher supplement that targets multiple health issuesCons: Only 60 tablets per jar, so long-term customers may need to reorder more often.

New Chapter Magnesium Bisglycinate Complex contains glycinate and provides 325 mg. It includes chelated bisglycinate, which supports high absorption, along with sea-sourced and fermented magnesium forms. New Chapter says it puts its supplements through third-party testing and validation, and this particular product is 100 percent vegan and kosher, making it suitable for those with dietary restrictions.

In a recent development, there isn’t a single magnesium dose that’s right for everyone, and more isn’t necessarily better. According to Ambardjieva, the recommended daily intake for adults is about 310 to 320 milligrams for women and 400 to 420 milligrams for men, including magnesium from both food and supplements. How much you may need from a supplement depends on your diet and individual health needs. When comparing products, look for the amount of elemental magnesium on the label rather than simply the total amount of the magnesium compound.

Taking too much supplemental magnesium can cause diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal cramping, while extremely high magnesium levels can lead to more serious problems, including effects on the heart and kidneys. People with a documented deficiency or those advised to supplement by a healthcare professional are the clearest candidates. If you’re unsure whether you need magnesium or which form and dose are appropriate, talk with a healthcare professional.

Magnesium supplements are generally well tolerated when taken appropriately, but higher amounts can cause digestive side effects, including nausea, diarrhea, or abdominal discomfort. The risk of side effects can also vary depending on the form of magnesium.

Because magnesium supplements can also interact with some medications, people taking prescription drugs or managing a medical condition should check with a healthcare professional before supplementing.

It has been revealed that we first interviewed Ambardjieva about magnesium, including which forms may be better absorbed, research-backed benefits, appropriate doses, deficiency symptoms, potential risks, and what consumers should look for in a quality supplement. We then researched available products and evaluated them based on magnesium form, elemental magnesium per serving, ingredient transparency, and serving size. We prioritized products containing forms discussed by the doctor and considered options for different preferences, including vegan, kosher, capsule, and powder formulations.

In a recent development, we also considered tolerability, since some forms and higher doses of magnesium may cause digestive side effects. We did not rely solely on marketing claims, popularity, or customer reviews when making our selections, and third-party testing was a priority for every product. Our picks reflect a combination of evidence, product quality, safety, and practical considerations rather than one-size-fits-all recommendations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon's Black Friday sale kicked off today, which means it's a good time to score some of the year's best prices on e-readers. Timing your purchase is now a bigger deal than ever (so to speak), as Amazon recently raised the price of basically every Kindle by $50 or more due to the ongoing RAM crisis.

Because of this, the prices aren't nearly as low as they were last year, but now is still the time to get a decent discount on a Kindle Paperwhite or Colorsoft—but if you'd rather read differently, you can also save substantial on a few worthy Kindle alternatives. Here are your e-reader best bets in the lead-up to Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

Recent findings suggest that the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is the best e-reader for most people. An upgraded version of the basic Kindle, the Paperwhite adds a larger screen, temperature-adjustable lighting, water resistance, and better battery life—and if you opt for the Signature Edition, you also get double the storage and no lock screen ads. Earlier this year, it jumped in price to $250, even before the company introduced a latest model—but you can get the 2024 model for $179.99, 28% off the new list price.

If you want a great Kindle but you don't care about paying extra for more storage or getting rid of lock screen ads, the non-Signature Edition of the Kindle Paperwhite is also a great buy right now. The 2024 model has been discounted to $129.99 from the list price of $199.99. It's available in standard black, Jade, or Raspberry colors.

If you don't need the bells and whistles of the Paperwhite, you can also pick up the standard Kindle. It's still a very capable device, with good lighting, 16GB of onboard storage, and the ability to hook up your Bluetooth speakers to listen to Audible audiobooks. The standard Kindle, which now retails for $150, is marked down to $119.99, making it the cheapest Kindle option. Though I think it makes more sense to spend $10 more on the Signature Edition, this is the way to go if you want the cute Matcha color.

If you like to read comics or you just appreciate looking at your book covers in full color, the 2024 Kindle Colorsoft is also at a strong 41% discount for Black Friday, bringing it down to around $170. For $10 less than the Paperwhite Signature edition, you get all the same perks (including an ad-free experience) and a color e-ink screen that's great for reading magazines, graphic novels, and manga. Color e-ink isn't for everyone, but if it's for you, the Colorsoft has the best color screen on the market. For an extra $10, the Colorsoft Kids Edition adds a case, a yearlong subscription to Kindle Kids+, and an extended warranty.

Sources indicate that if you're looking for a combination e-reader and e-notebook, the Kindle Scribe is a great option. With a larger screen than Amazon's other e-readers, it offers all the benefits of the Paperwhite but adds support for the excellent Premium Pen stylus, allowing you to take notes in your Amazon e-books or create handwritten documents that you can later convert to text using the onboard AI tools. The 32GB black-and-white version of the Kindle Scribe is currently $349.99, while the Colorsoft version will run you $449.99. Both of these are the newest models, released in 2025.

The new Kindle Scribe Colorsoft has all the same great features of the black-and-white version discussed above, but adds a full-color e-ink display. Combined with the large 11-inch screen, this makes it a great device for reading comics or magazine articles as they were meant to be read, or marking up PDFs using the included Premium Pen. This device usually costs a hefty $630, but the current Black Friday sale cuts $180 off of that price.

According to recent reports, if you want to step outside of the Amazon ecosystem, the Kobo Libra Colour is a good bet. Discounted $30 to $229.99 at Best Buy, it's currently pricier than the Kindle Colorsoft, but you get a bit more for your money. While most of the specs are similar (they both use the same Kaleido 3 screen and offer 32GB of storage), the Kobo supports a stylus, so you can jot down notes in your books or keep a digital journal. It also has physical page-turn buttons, which the Colorsoft lacks.

According to recent reports, if you don't want to be tied to the Amazon ecosystem and/or you're looking for a device that's a bit more portable, consider the Viwoods AiPaper Reader, currently marked down to $200, its lowest price ever. It's got a 6.13-inch screen, so it's the same size and shape as your phone, and it has a crisp e-ink screen with a strong (if not temperature-adjustable) front light and 128GB of onboard storage. The best part is, it runs on an open Android system, so you can install multiple reading apps, including Kindle, Nook, Kobo, and Libby, and keep all of your books in one place. (Check out my review of the Viwoods AiPaper Reader for more—it's a nifty little device.).

If you don't have a large Kindle library, you're moderately tech-savvy, and you praise portability above all else, I can't recommend Xteink's line of e-readers more highly. The 4.3-inch Xteink X4 Classic is at its lowest price ever, coming in at just under $55, around $34 off the list price. Meanwhile, the smaller 3.7-inch Xteink X3 is about a dollar more; that's a less-generous 19% discount. I own both, and while the Classic is definitely worth the current sale price, I actually prefer the form factor of the smaller X3 (currently $55.72), which is about the size of a library card.

According to recent reports, for about $30 more than the X4 Classic, you can upgrade to the Xteink X4 Pro, which happens to be Lifehacker's e-reader Gift of the Year pick. It offers all the perks of the other Xteink devices, with two critical quality-of-life upgrades: A touchscreen for easier navigation, and a temperature-adjustable front light so you can read it in a dark room. (Less obviously, it also has a slightly faster processor that makes the whole thing feel a little snappier.) Right now, the X4 Pro is at its lowest price ever when ordered directly from Xteink: $84, or around 15% off the usual $99 price.

If you're feeling tentative about trusting a seemingly no-name Chinese tech brand, read more about the devices in my review, or listen to the collected wisdom of the tens of thousands of people in the bustling r/xteink Reddit group.

It has been revealed that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Investigatory Powers Tribunal – essentially a British court that deals with complaints about state surveillance – has ruled that Apple is allowed to reveal a secret order it received from the UK government.

Apple had already found a clever way to alert British customers to the classified order without breaking the law, but it can now confirm what we all already knew, and talk openly about the concern ….

According to recent reports, the story centers on Apple’s introduction of the Advanced Data Protection (ADP) privacy feature back in 2022. This extended end-to-end encryption to almost all your iCloud data, meaning Apple has no access, and therefore cannot grant access to any government agencies who come knocking on its door.

Sources indicate that the feature is off by default because it means Apple cannot help you access any of your data if, for example, you forget your iCloud password. However, those who want to maximize the privacy of their iCloud account can enable it.

Recent findings suggest that in 2025, the British government ordered Apple to create a backdoor to allow access by security services and law enforcement. Even worse, the order was issued under legislation that prohibits companies from revealing that they have received this demand.

Recent findings suggest that this would have meant that British customers who enabled ADP would think that their data was safe when in fact it wasn’t. As we’ve stated many times before, any backdoor created for use by the good guys is vulnerable to discovery and exploitation by the bad guys.

According to recent reports, it would have been illegal for Apple to reveal that it had been instructed to compromise the privacy of customer data, but the firm found a clever way to effectively communicate this without breaking the law. Apple announced it was withdrawing ADP from the UK without explaining its reason.

It has been revealed that “Apple can no longer offer Advanced Data Protection (ADP) in the United Kingdom to new consumers and current UK users will eventually need to disable this security feature. ADP protects iCloud data with end-to-end encryption, which means the data can only be decrypted by the user who owns it, and only on their trusted devices. We are gravely disappointed that the protections provided by ADP will not be available to our customers in the UK […] As we have noted many times before, we have never built a backdoor or master key to any of our products or services and we never will.”.

Tell me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP without telling me you’ve been ordered to create a backdoor to ADP ….

At this point, it was an open secret. However, ridiculously, despite the fact that everyone in the security and privacy field knew about it and was talking about it, Apple was still not allowed to officially confirm it.

Recent findings suggest that the iPhone maker asked the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) to allow it to openly discuss the order, with privacy campaigners backing this call. The Financial Times reports that the court has now ruled in Apple’s favor.

The UK government must admit that it issued a secret order to Apple to allow it access to encrypted customer data, a court has ruled […] The Home Office has “not established that it would be damaging to national security” to reveal that Apple had received a “technical capability notice” (TCN), the tribunal said. The ruling means that […] “much” of Apple and the non-profits’ legal challenge can now take place in open court.

One of the great ironies is that most people had never heard of ADP until the government effectively made it headline news in the tech press three years after it debuted – a classic example of the Streisand Effect.

According to recent reports, this ruling is a win both for transparency and commonsense. To be clear, the actual requirement for a backdoor remains in place, but this can now be challenged in open court.

#165648. Latest Update: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

Latest Update: How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2962 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • Sources indicate that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

Sources indicate that last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

The tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

This mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

Sources indicate that “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” claims Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

In a recent development, phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Sources indicate that scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

Recent findings suggest that more than 10 years in the making, MMX launched on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a new rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

Recent findings suggest that MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

Sources indicate that if all goes according to strategy, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” claims Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

It has been revealed that once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to initiative, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” notes Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

The best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

During its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

Sources indicate that before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu notes, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

It will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

Sources indicate that idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

“It will bounce probably several times,” indicates Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation shows how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Industry observers note that once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she says. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

It has been revealed that the team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday says.

In a recent development, despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday indicates Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Idefix’s interactions with its fresh home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec indicates. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

What Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Recent findings suggest that once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

It has been revealed that the MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

Industry observers note that the coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Sources indicate that probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this matter and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu says.

One of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

Industry observers note that that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

According to recent reports, during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

Once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Industry observers note that finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

“We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel indicates. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

“MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu claims. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Diplomat is a show that loves mess (complimentary). Kate Wyler (Keri Russel) is a mess in many ways, and almost every major character is at emotional, moral, or intellectual loose ends. This would all be in good fun if these characters weren’t also some of the most powerful people in the world—presidents, prime ministers, and the high-level politicians and diplomats that serve them.

If you’ve been following the Wylers’ emotional journey up the power ladder as Kate navigates her role as the U.S. ambassador to the United Kingdom during what could be described as tumultuous times (and you’ve watched all our series streamalikes), allow me to suggest the one perfect movie that delivers similar vibes: 2009's In the Loop.

Released in 2009, In the Loop doesn’t have the modern edge of The Diplomat, but it perfectly captures a similar sense that international diplomacy is being conducted by people with an affinity for chaos. It’s actually a spinoff from a British TV series from the same co-writer/director, Armando Iannucci: The Thick of It. Many of the characters and situations are based on some of the people actually running the U.K., but you don’t need to be familiar with the show or the real history to enjoy the heck out of this movie. That goes double for Peter Capaldi’s absolutely ferocious performance as Malcolm Tucker, a man so creative with his profanity that many of his F-bombs will live rent-free in your head for years to come.

When a not-so-bright minister in the U.K. government (played by Tom Hollander) makes some dimwitted remarks that threaten to blow up Britain's carefully crafted diplomatic messaging around potential military adventures in the Middle East, Tucker (the prime minister's director of communications) has to tamp down the growing chaos that results. This eventually requires a contingent of British diplomats and officials to head to Washington, where they are promptly overwhelmed by the superpower vibes they encounter.

It’s a more profane, faster-paced, and outright comedic story than The Diplomat, but it’s also easy to imagine most of the characters showing up on that show. The film also shares that same sense of controlled chaos that drives The Diplomat—the idea that a handful of tired, dedicated people are continuously racing around to prevent World War III even as dumber and more powerful people keep creating new crises. If Kate Wyler’s constant state of exhausted anxiety is your jam, you’ll love this movie. Stream In the Loop on The Roku Channel, Kanopy, or Plex, or rent it on Prime Video.

Want more cynical diplomats, secret prepares, and international skulduggery with a side of personal emotional crises? Here are a few more movies fans of The Diplomat will love.

If you want a sense of what actual back-channel diplomacy is like, watch Ben Affleck’s Best Picture winner Argo, from 2012. Based on the remarkable true story of how six U.S. diplomats were rescued from Tehran during the Iran Hostage Crisis under cover of a fake sci-fi movie production, the film has the snappy energy and fast pace of The Diplomat combined with real-world danger. You can easily imagine Kate and Hal (Rufus Sewell) being part of the secret, off-the-books conversations that brought what’s known as the Canadian Caper into reality. Stream Argo on Paramount Plus or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that if your favorite parts of The Diplomat are the schemes various players (mostly Kate and Hal) get up to in their efforts to shape world diplomacy and history to their liking, Wag the Dog is a good bet. When a sex scandal threatens to swing the Presidential election away from the incumbent, a spin doctor (Robert De Niro) wades in to save the day by convincing a top Hollywood producer (Dustin Hoffman) to “produce” a fake war in Albania to distract the American public. It’s equal parts funny, compelling, and depressingly instructive, and fans of the show will love the back-channel hijinks. Rent Wag the Dog on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that one of the great things about The Diplomat is watching Kate Wyler, a smart and capable woman who generally knows more than anyone else in the room. If that’s the dynamic that grabs you, The Contender is the overlooked gem for you. When the vice president dies unexpectedly, the President (Jeff Bridges) nominates Senator Laine Hanson (Joan Allen) to take the post. A conservative senator (Gary Oldman) opposes her nomination and launches a smear campaign to derail her confirmation. There are dirty tricks and secret deals, and in the middle of it all, Allen’s terrific performance as a woman who refuses to back down in the face of sexist, unfair attacks. Stream The Contender on The Roku Channel, Kanopy, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Apple TV.

In a recent development, nicole Kidman plays an interpreter at the United Nations, a woman who has a unique heritage and linguistic knowledge. When she overhears an assassination plot in an obscure dialect, she becomes embroiled in a dangerous game of espionage and high-stakes diplomacy as she races to prevent disaster (and keep herself alive). The Interpreter is a more serious and much more tense story, but it delves into the background work that makes the global system function, which puts it right in the sweet spot for fans of The Diplomat. Stream The Interpreter on Netflix, or rent it on Prime Video.

This might not seem like a match at first glance—a comedic treatment of the power struggle that followed the death of Soviet Premier Josef Stalin in 1953—but it absolutely is. Making a farce out of the political wrangling among the members of the Central Committee, the film has the same spirit as The Diplomat, showing that the people in charge are a bunch of schemers, tricksters, dummies, and sociopaths. Watching them run around making deals and angling for advantage offers the same energy as the show. Plus, it’s just plain hilarious. Stream The Death of Stalin on Kanopy, or rent it on Prime Video.

Pairing with an iPhone or iPad running the iOS or iPadOS 27.3 beta may cause Siri requests to fail.

As discovered by pdfu, if you try to make a Personal Content request on an iPhone running iOS 27.3, Siri in HomeView 27.2.1 now states: “I can’t help with that because your personal device is on newer software.”.

Sources indicate that if you’re on iOS 27.3, Siri on HomeView can’t use your iPhone for personal context, likely until December.HomeView won’t send Siri requests to an iPhone on newer software. It’s understandable that problems might arise from having iOS and HomeView software that’s out of sync. Unfortunately though, there’s no beta software available for HomeView at the moment.

That means unless Apple releases a beta soon, owners might have to wait until the public launch of HomeView 27.3 in December to get Personal Content features back.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

During Monday’s game between the Toronto Maple Leafs and Upcoming York Islanders, Broadway performer Sarrah Strimel Bentley flubbed the lyrics to Canada‘s national anthem multiple times before the puck drop.

When singing “O Canada” for the thousands of fans during the Islanders’ Hockey Fights Cancer night, instead of belting out, “O Canada, we stand on guard for thee,” Bentley repeatedly sang, “O Canada, we lend our hearts to thee.”.

The singer also missed the mark on another line, and instead of singing, “True patriot love in all of us command,” she sang, “True patriot love with all of us command.”.

In a recent development, A clip from the performance showed Leafs captain Auston Matthews appearing confused as she sang the wrong lyrics. The anthem blunder drew swift criticism from hockey and Canadian fans online. Trending Stories Billy Ray Cyrus Shares Snapshots From Miley’s Wedding: 'Beautiful' to See Family 'United by Love' Watch Taylor Swift Surprise Brenda Lee With ‘Rockin’ Around the Christmas Tree’ Honor Previously Unseen Footage of Led Zeppelin at Madison Square Garden Surfaces After 49 Years Anthem Singer Apologizes for ‘O Canada’ Flub at Leafs-Islanders Game.

Auston Matthews’ reaction to the Canadian national anthem being sung wrong is incredible 😭“We lend our hearts to thee” 🤨#leafs pic.twitter.com/Ar59glBfGS.

Later that night, Bentley took to social media to apologize in a video. “I sang both anthems, and I just wanted to apologize to all of my Canadians,” Bentley began. “Because I practiced the shit out of ‘O Canada,’ and getting up in front of 18,000 people, singing an anthem that you haven’t heard for your whole life is scary, and I botched the lyrics, and I’m really sorry. I got put in menopause because I had breast cancer, and tonight is about hockey fighting cancer, and menopause makes you forget things.”.

Recent findings suggest that bentley continued, “So, I just wish that you’d be a little easier on someone who’s just a human being. And I’m sorry.” The singer highlighted the correct lyrics in her apology video: “Thank you for giving me grace. I love Canada. I stand on guard for thee.”.

  • The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027.
  • “Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that microsoft is saying goodbye to its task management service To Do, including the Mac and iOS apps. Here’s what consumers need to know.

The last day to use the To Do apps is June 30, 2027. That date also applies to Windows, Android, and the web. The underlying service and sync support will retire later, according to Microsoft’s support document.

“Microsoft To Do is retiring,” Microsoft explains. “For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.”.

On the Mac, you can use Planner on the web or in Teams. Microsoft explicitly says it has no looks for a native Mac app.

According to recent reports, you can still see your existing To Do tasks in Planner through June 30, but your tasks and lists won’t carry over. Microsoft looks to offer an export option before the apps retire.

Planner doesn’t support personal Microsoft accounts however. If that’s how you use To Do, you’ll need to pick another task manager, even if you pay for Microsoft 365 Personal or Family, according to the firm.

In a recent development, the June shutdown will end a run of just over a decade for To Do on Apple platforms. Microsoft bought the manufacturer behind Wunderlist in 2015 and released the first iPhone preview of To Do in April 2017.

Looking for a proper replacement? Apple’s built-in Reminders app can keep lists in sync between Apple devices, including a grocery list you share with family through iCloud.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft has been trying to make Teams as the super app for some time now, as Planner is integrated into Teams. Teams is one of the prime examples of why super apps are terrible, with a bloated, web app-like experience.

If you liked To Do because it worked across platforms, Todoist has apps for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Windows, and Android.

Sources indicate that does this sunsetting affect you? Were you a Wunderlist user back in the day? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Update: Howard Crow, Director of Product, Agents and AI, Microsoft, shared this statement with 9to5Mac regarding the transition:.

“We’re bringing task management experiences together across Microsoft 365 to make it easier for customers to manage individual tasks and team plans. As part of this transition, Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027, with work and school experiences coming together in Microsoft Planner. Existing integrations across Microsoft 365, including Outlook and Teams, will also be updated to work with Planner. We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare. Customers will be able to export their To Do data before retirement, and we’ll share additional guidance to support the transition.”.
