The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz, and the glasses support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling and billions of colors, all in a package that weighs only 62 grams. It can be hard to buy a gift for a health-focused person. They usually don't want booze and they like putting in effort. It's more versatile than a watch (you can wear it on your bicep and even in your underwear) and it monitors heart rate, respiratory rate, heart rate variability, skin temperature, blood oxygen levels, daily activity, and sleep—basically everything I don't worry about. You cannot go wrong with a GoPro. The tech giant's easy-to-use, hard-to-break cameras are synonymous with "action photography" and compact enough to fit in a stocking. Even if your giftee isn't an adventurer, the GoPro Hero 13 supports additional lenses and filters that let people go beyond the "gnarly fish-eye, dude" photography and videography of past generations. Check out associate tech editor Michelle Ehrhardt's GoPro Hero 13 review for more details.

Sources indicate that everyone wants their own droid. Beni from Mondo Robotics is a camera robot that takes 4K video while autonomously following its subject wherever they go. If you want to get action footage, there's no need to hassle with a tripod or another person: You can control Beni with the remote, or simply tell it to follow you. It can be set to track you from behind, from the side, or it can circle you, and you can adjust what it is doing from the app or remote on the fly, so there's no limit to the kind of elaborate shots it can pull off. Plus it's freakin' adorable. The $799 list price might be a bit steep for most gift-givers, but as far as how well it works and how much fun I've had using it, it's worth the money.

Industry observers note that the R36 Max 2 retro handheld game console lets you take your gaming anywhere. It comes with over 20,000 games pre-installed, so you can play every title from classic consoles like the Atari 2600 or the PlayStation 1, as well as just about every arcade game anyone ever dropped a coin into, all for less than $100. I paid more than that in quarters just to beat Dragon's Lair!

I'm obsessed with the Yamaha Seqtrak. It crams a drum machine, sequencer, sampler, three separate synthesizers, and a speaker into a package small enough to put into a Christmas stocking. It's a complete mobile studio—everything you need to produce a song or beat—but it also integrates with your computer's DAW and other MIDI gear to become part of your home studio. All that for only $300!

According to recent reports, the Flipper Zero is a must-have device for the hardcore, glasses-wearing, circuit-bender type of techie. Its ability to do evil deeds like hack ATMs is greatly exaggerated, but the Flipper is still a technological Swiss Army knife that lets you read and manipulate the invisible waves around you, from radio waves to RFID, NFC, Bluetooth, and wifi signals. It's educational, fascinating, and powerful; how you use that power is your business.

If you're giving a gift to a would-be Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, this miniature, wireless microscope will rock their holiday. It's easy to set up, works with PCs, Android, or iOS devices, magnifies things up to 1000x, and takes 1080p pictures of your discoveries.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then indicates how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

10 Hacks Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1242 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far.
  • Sources indicate that I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are key.
  • If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far. The world feels even more detailed and immersive than previous GTA games, which means there's a lot to learn beyond the basic tutorials and prompts the game shares at the beginning. These are the 10 GTA 6 hacks I used to improve the game's quality of life. If you do the same, you'll spend more time immersed in the world, and less time fighting the game's default settings.

Sources indicate that I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are key. If you ignore all the optional quests or small asks by other characters, you won't be able to return to those later. These are small things like fixing up the house for Lucia, meditating with her, and buying her a necklace when she asks you to. All of these have an impact on your progress. Take your time in this chapter, and remember to save before starting the mission called "Recalibration." That mission leads to Tourist Trap, which is the point of no return for Chapter 1.

If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different. It's hard to keep an eye on minimap directions while you're also getting used to vehicles in the game, and I used voice navigation to ensure that I don't keep getting lost, particularly for time-sensitive missions. You can enable this by going to GTA VI settings > Audio > GPS Voice > Voice. If you're playing the game on PS5, your DualSense controller's speaker plays GPS voice prompts. This is great as those alerts can be hard to hear over all other in-game sounds from your TV's speaker.

Using GTA 6's default controls, making Jason and Lucia run is quite annoying. The game makes you hold L3 to run, which hurts my thumbs. If you alter movement speed in settings, you can make the characters run just by using the left stick. You can walk by easing off the left stick, or switch to a fast walk, jog, or run when you push the stick all the way. Tweak this by going to GTA VI settings > Gameplay > Movement Speed > Jog. This lets you move faster without draining your stamina. You can also change from Jog to Run if you want the fastest possible movement speed with the left stick. Having mentioned that, my pro tip is to go to Control Scheme in settings, and switch to Classic. This lets you run by holding the X button, as opposed to L3 with default controls.

Sources indicate that haptic strength is one area where GTA 6 takes the immersion a bit too far, as it's dialed up to the maximum level by default. This makes the controller's vibration strength a bit too intense for my liking, and also has a negative impact on battery life. You can fix that by reducing haptic strength a little. It's under GTA VI settings > Controller > Vibration & Haptics Strength.

Recent findings suggest that many modern controllers develop "stick drift," an concern where small movements of the analog sticks register as large inputs. This causes a big problem in games that require precise inputs, such as GTA 6. To counter this potential problem, the game allows you to adjust the deadzone for each analog stick in your controller. That said, this setting can be used to your advantage, even if you don't have stick drift issues in your controller. I recommend dialing up the deadzone to 7 to improve the driving experience. I find most cars in GTA 6 to be a bit floaty to drive, and adjusting the deadzone fixes this issue to a large extent.

Committing a heist attracts heat in GTA 6, and there are many different ways to escape the attention of in-game cops. The usual tricks include stocking up on outfits to change into, parking your vehicle a block or two away, and being so stealthy that you leave no witnesses to your crimes. However, an underrated trick involves using the pickup truck you get at the start of the game. Get a bike in the game, and stash it in your pickup truck. Then, use the truck to drive to the crime scene, and hide the truck a short distance away. Unload the bike, and use it to get to the crime scene. Once the heist is complete, ditch the bike, and run to your truck. Witnesses won't have seen you using the truck, which allows you to escape the area swiftly.

In a recent development, if you are using a car as a getaway vehicle, you can use two tricks to make a smooth escape. First, double-tap the Triangle button to exit your vehicle without switching off its engine. When you return to the vehicle in a hurry, you can escape a lot faster. If you have quick fingers, you can double-tap Triangle first, and just as your character is about to exit the vehicle, press L3 (or X, if you use classic controls). This leaves the car's door open, and saves you a little more time when you're fleeing.

I suffer from chronic migraines, and I am sensitive to bright lights. Fortunately, GTA 6 has a bunch of accessibility settings that help me play the game for longer. Even if you don't face the same complications, these settings will help reduce eye strain in longer play sessions. Go to GTA VI settings > Display > Flashbang, and switch to Dark. This stops flashbangs from showing a bright white light when they go off. On the same settings page, you can tweak Player Status Effects Intensity to reduce screen effects when your character is low on health or stamina. You can also enable Brightness Reduction to reduce the intensity of bright lights in the game, and try Focus Trail Colorblind Mode if you find it hard to distinguish between different colors.

I haven't been able to play first-person shooters for decades because the camera movement makes me nauseous and gives me a headache. Of late, I've noticed that it's getting harder to play third-person games too. My first two hours in GTA 6 had me quite worried because I was feeling quite sick, and I had to turn off my PS5. Luckily for me, I found a few tweaks to mitigate this problem. You can do that in GTA VI settings > UI > Persistent Center Dot. This permanently indicates a white dot in the center of the screen, and it reduced my motion sickness enough to help me play the game. You can also go to GTA VI settings > Camera, reduce Camera Bob, and turn off Camera Shake, and Weapon Sway. I also recommend going to the Controller tab in settings, and tweaking all the options under Aim & Look Sensitivity until you find a comfortable level.

GTA 6 includes realistic ringing sounds that linger after explosions in the game. This may be fine for some people, but it can negatively affect some players' gaming sessions. Those who suffer from tinnitus or chronic migraines may not enjoy those ringing sounds, and, luckily, the game allows you to disable them. Open GTA 6's in-game settings, and enable the feature from Audio > Tinnitus Reduction.

In a recent development, but Adaptive Audio is another option you may or may not have tried. The feature aims to blend the strengths of both ANC and Transparency in a single mode.

And in iOS 27, Apple added a fresh setting to let you conveniently fine-tune Adaptive Audio to your preferences.

According to recent reports, while wearing AirPods, open Control Center on your iPhone and tap the volume slider, then hit ‘Listening Mode’ in the bottom-left corner. Here you’ll see the standard listening mode options.

New in iOS 27 though, when ‘Adaptive’ is selected, you can now use a Liquid Glass slider to adjust whether the mode lets in more or less external noise.

Slide it to the left and Adaptive Audio will more closely resemble Transparency, while sliding it to the right makes it cancel out more noise.

You can also move the new slider incrementally to achieve exactly your ideal balance of Transparency and Noise Cancellation. It’s not limited to just a few preset options.

This Control Center slider is available on all AirPods models that support Adaptive Audio.

Recent findings suggest that 9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

In a recent development, mark Gurman reports that Apple hasn’t named a newly introduced vice president to replace McCormack, who reported to software chief Craig Federighi. “Instead, his former deputies are assuming his responsibilities under other executives,” the report indicates.

In his role, McCormack oversaw “close coordination between software engineers and Apple’s camera hardware and chip teams.” He’s credited with last year’s redesigned selfie camera and other projects:.

His work included the redesigned selfie camera introduced with the iPhone 17 lineup last year. This year, Apple added a variable-aperture camera to the iPhone 18 Pro lineup, giving people more control over lighting and depth of field. The manufacturer also introduced a customizable Camera app interface with professional controls.

Bloomberg describes McCormack as a “strong opponent of using generative AI to create or alter photographs,” a philosophy that created tension as Apple embraced AI tools in the Photos app. His retirement, however, “wasn’t related to a disagreement or clash with Apple over its AI strategy,” the report claims.

McCormack spoke in depth about iOS 27 features like Clean Up, Extend, and Spatial Reframing in an interview with Tyler Stalman in June. He emphasized how the features “preserve the integrity of the moment.”.

#165624. ‘Fin Vs History’: Stars Of Video Podcast On The Wildly-Popular Satirical History Series, Animation Ambitions & Why Spotify Beats TV

‘Fin Vs History’: Stars Of Video Podcast On The Wildly-Popular Satirical History Series, Animation Ambitions & Why Spotify Beats TV

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2226 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Deadline

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • EXCLUSIVE: For Fin Taylor, one half of the satirical podcast Fin Vs History, there’s no going back to TV now.
  • The British stand-up comedian, writer and podcaster, who fronts his show with fellow comedian Horatio Gould, had over the years made appearances on staple British comedy shows such as Live at the Apollo and The Last Leg, but his deliberately shocking style didn’t feel like a good fit – to him.
  • It has been revealed that as we sit down for lunch at the Ham Yard Hotel in London, he recalls making a VT for BBC news satire The Mash Report that had been cut so severely that it made his deliberately anti-woke character seemed more “fascist” than a satirical take on a news reporter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: For Fin Taylor, one half of the satirical podcast Fin Vs History, there’s no going back to TV now.

The British stand-up comedian, writer and podcaster, who fronts his show with fellow comedian Horatio Gould, had over the years made appearances on staple British comedy shows such as Live at the Apollo and The Last Leg, but his deliberately shocking style didn’t feel like a good fit – to him.

It has been revealed that as we sit down for lunch at the Ham Yard Hotel in London, he recalls making a VT for BBC news satire The Mash Report that had been cut so severely that it made his deliberately anti-woke character seemed more “fascist” than a satirical take on a news reporter. He was livid. Related Stories Executives Reed Hastings On Netflix Shakeup, YouTube Rivalry And How Streamer Can Go Back To "Being Thrilling" News Sue Perkins Exploring ADHD Diagnosis For First Time In Audible Podcast 'Attention, Please! Tales From A Distracted Mind'.

It has been revealed that “This was during Covid, when agents weren’t allowed to come to the record,” he recalls. “I went into the gallery and I threw my toys out of the pram, and said, ‘You can’t use that in the show.’ I had basically accepted I wouldn’t be asked back, but weirdly they called the next morning and apologized, and they got me to write more stuff for them.” Watch on Deadline.

Even though that worked out, the incident was one of several that made Taylor seek out a different path. There was also a wild broadcast where he was asked to give the British perspective on NFL Network’s Good Morning Football, leading to what can only be described as mayhem and the naming of his company, Fumblerooski Productions. Watch the video below for context on that.

Sources indicate that taylor knew that his television future would be “the funny guy on a show that’s not comedy, like Sewing Bee,” but says: “They’re never going to book me to do that because I’m a bull in a China shop. They’re not putting me on The Great British Bake Off. I needed to do my own thing.”.

Sources indicate that for Gould, a comedian’s life as a TV star felt even more alien. “I didn’t see anything on TV that I would want to do, or would want me,” he indicates. Both men had been active on the UK stand-up scene, but Gould, who’s slightly younger than his podcast partner, natively posted his comedy online, and he was sure his future was more likely in digital self-publishing than on the BBC or ITV.

Recent findings suggest that “We all looked over to America, which is always five years ahead,” says Gould. “There were so many comedians doing video podcasts and indicates it was only a matter of time before it came over here.”.

Soon Taylor, Gould and Irish comedian Vittorio Angelone had devised Fin Vs the Internet, an online comedy series vehicle for Taylor in which he would play a deluded interviewer determined to find out why those he spoke with had bigger and better online followings than he did.

“He was like a Between Two Ferns-meets-Eric Andre character, who has no idea how the internet works and has views of a man from the ’50s,” indicates Gould, who wrote and produced the show, but remained off screen. “These were people who are very careful about their brands and he was like a bulldozer,” adds Taylor.

Guests included YouTube star JaackMaate, comedian and OnlyFans performer Rebecca Goodwin, reality star and podcaster Jamie Laing, and Love Island contestant Chris Williamson, whose podcast Taylor and Gould have appeared on directly before we meet. (That episode published online yesterday.) Four seasons of the show ran between 2022 and 2024, and an accompanying Patreon podcast was created.

Then a little twist of fate led to Fin Vs History. Taylor and Gould – British men who both have history degrees – had recently been to Ireland, so they decided to film themselves talking about the country’s history without doing any proper research, primarily to troll Angelone, an Irish stand-up comic. “That went really well, and it was actually exciting to do,” states Taylor. “Vittorio was starting a tour and we did a few more of them, and then we started realizing the clicks were going nuts.”.

It has been revealed that however, it was clear even at this stage a paywalled production could not last in the long term. “The Patreon podcast didn’t really work,” indicates Gould. “The idea was we wanted to keep giving people weekly stuff to pay for a web series that took ages to make.” However, this period ended up serving as “perfect development” for what eventually released in January 2025 as Fin Vs History.

In a recent development, angelone, who had his own podcast, amicably stepped aside (“He’s now our IRA correspondent,” indicates Taylor), while Gould had to square the time drain of another production alongside his popular Boys Gone Wild video podcast show – and potentially a continuation of the Patreon podcast. The latter was scrapped and the focus went entirely on creating Fin Vs History.

Taylor’s Fumblerooski Productions, which he runs with exec producer Pete Wells (“the George Martin figure,” as they call him), took on production and Podmasters, the UK-based independent podcast network, signed it to help expand the audience and monetize the show.

Gould was obsessed with Brian McGee, an aged 1970s BBC presenter and philosopher who presented stuffy, hour-long TV conversations, and felt this should be the aesthetic for a comedy show satirising history academics.

“He was this very bored, ancient-looking professor of philosophy, who would just sit on a beige sofa for an hour in front of a beige background with an even older guy with an even more dandruff-flecked suit, and they would talk about Wittgenstein.”.

Accordingly, each episode sees Taylor and Gould sitting facing each other in ill-fitting, bunching suits or military regalia, including hats they rent from the National Theatre. “We have a whole tailoring operation,” says Taylor as an aside. “The sofa means you can’t help but be in this funny position,” adds Gould. “It would not be as funny if we were on a sofa in just our trackies.”.

According to recent reports, taylor and Gould take on the personas of two out-of-touch history buffs with extremely questionable views on almost every issue and every part of history, often taking the side of the very worst people and views in human history. “‘Hitler: Friend of the pod’ is the fundamental joke,” says Gould, explaining their characters’ warped worldviews.

Fin Vs History is deliberately provocative and certainly shocking to the unsuspecting listeners – and some have called the podcast right-leaning, though its creators say it is a staunchly non-political show and purely there to find the next laugh. “It is about doing everything you shouldn’t do, whilst dressed as if you really care about it,” explains Taylor. “I trust that if you don’t find that funny, you just won’t listen to it. If you listen to the episodes, it is genuinely impossible not to understand that nothing in it is sincere.”.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s what’s great about internet TV,” adds Gould. “Back in the day, you would go into someone’s home and you had certain responsibilities and had to cater to the audience. We are in a corner of the internet putting our stuff out.”.

“We’re in an old lawn bowls club in Anerley. Why are you here?” quips Taylor, slipping effortlessly into his curmudgeonly character.

Since launching in early 2025, Fin Vs History has exploded in popularity, surpassing 66 million downloads with deep-dive series on the likes of Horatio Nelson, pirates, Roman Emperors, the Russian revolution, the Nazis and World War II, Ugandan dictator Idi Amin and, more quirkily, a much-loved episode on the 2018 Thai cave rescue. It won a Chortle Award, sold put the O2 Shepherd’s Bush Empire with a live show and was nominated for Best Comedy Podcast at the British Podcast Awards.

According to recent reports, on Spotify, it currently ranks as the 12th most-popular video podcast in the UK, behind the likes of The Rest is History, on which the show shares topical DNA, and The Joe Rogan Experience. Serendipity played a part there: The show began booming just as music service Spotify went all-out on video podcasting to compete with YouTube. “Because we started doing well, they started to push us more as their success story,” says Taylor. “We did get lucky on the timing.”.

According to recent reports, “Fin vs History is exactly the kind of show we love at Podmasters,” Martin Bojtos, co-founder and CEO of Podmasters upon re-signing the pod in September. “It is original, fearless and completely distinctive. To see it grow at this speed has been incredible, but what means just as much is that Fin, Horatio and the team have chosen to continue that journey with us. For us, that trust is a real measure of success.”.

“I always had the sense I wanted to be funded by lots of people paying little things rather than one brand paying a lot,” says Gould of the business model. “It means you can do what you want. Piss off one person, that’s £3 [$3.90].” Taylor finishes his thought: “Piss off one brand, £10,000.”.

Gould does worry that the exponential growth towards a more mainstream audience could lead to the nuance of the underlying joke of Fin Vs History being lost, but Taylor takes a different view – there will be a ceiling to the audience.

“It was never supposed to be mainstream in the way we’re talking about stuff,” he notes. “We’re always going to be in The Rest is History’s shadow because that is mainstream. The Rest is History is so major that you can subvert it and still be one of the biggest podcasts in the country. I genuinely think if you come to Fin Vs History not knowing why it’s funny, you don’t find it funny.”.

Recent findings suggest that the Fin vs History podcast, via Taylor’s Fumblerooski, and Gould are separately both represented by CAA, which has been heavily pushing into the creator space in the UK since last year, as we reported back in December 2025. Gould is also managed by 42 for film and TV.

They share an agent, Glenn Miller, whose team are seeking to expand the brand – CAA’s Harriet Pollard led a five-way auction for Taylor’s debut book, The History of Mankind in its Entirety, earlier this year. The satirical book, written in the same voice as Taylor’s podcast version of himself, published in September.

According to recent reports, “CAA basically seeks to exploit the IP we make,” states Taylor. “They’re always looking for opportunities with the streamers for podcasts. The old way felt you couldn’t start anything because the ratings had to be part of it from the start, and now we’re just doing what we want, and the agent might say, ‘Hey, I can do X to your earnings.’ For me, that’s a much better way round where it still feels like it’s me, but there’s someone there maximizing it.”.

The future for the podcast includes animation, which it has experimented with in some episodes. “We have long-term animation ambitions, and we’re building out that side of it,” says Taylor, who adds: “The writing team we’re a part of and have accumulated would be perfect for an animated sitcom, which [British] TV was never able to do.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The key is being able to turn something around with no red tape, basically,” adds Gould. “That’s why South Park works so well. They’ve got this production line that feels so free.”.

Gould notes there have been discussions for a travel-themed Fin Vs offshoot, and is open to “any medium we can turn this show into,” while Taylor says upcoming productions would be contingent on Fumblerookski continuing to build. “I only want to do certain topics when our animation capabilities are ready,” he explains. “Video podcasting is so new and the resources are coming in.”.

Industry observers note that as our lunch at Ham Yard comes to a close, the conversation turns back to the nature of traditional broadcasting. Taylor recalls a BBC radio appearance that left him cold, and says Fin Vs History has proven he only wants to engage in projects in which he makes executive decisions, while Gould says the video podcast “is TV now,” and that the medium “can be anything – we used to open with sketches, just to experiment.”.

Taylor believes Fin Vs History represents “the perfect vehicle for creativity as comics who love history, and adds: “I just want it to keep being creative and not to feel like it’s becoming formulaic and stale, and I like the idea there will be another show borne out of this one. What’s nice is it’s all down to us.”.

For Taylor and Gould, TV is more likely on their list of historical subjects to cover than a pathway for the future.

Apple AirPods Pro 3 are not only my favorite earbuds I've ever owned, they might also be my favorite headphones of all time. The Pros sound great, come with excellent noise cancellation and transparency modes, and are packed with modern features that go beyond listening to music. I'd recommend these to any Apple user looking for the best overall audio experience at full price, but when they're $100 off, I actively encourage you to buy these now.

Industry observers note that on the surface, Apple's third-generation AirPods Pro are among the best ways to listen to audio on your Apple devices. The earbuds sound great: I'm not an audiophile or a headphone reviewer, but to my ears, the Pros deliver excellent sound quality, with plenty of bass and great sound separation. I frequently turn to mine when I want to pay close attention to a fresh album, or watch a show or movie with intricate sound design. Plus, like other AirPods, the Pros are great for jumping between your various Apple devices. I'm constantly switching between my iPhone, Mac, and Apple TV with mine, and they seamlessly move between each—at least, most of the time.

Industry observers note that the noise cancellation on these AirPods is also stellar. I used to take my AirPods Max with me on planes, but lately, I've been fine with just my Pros, since the noise cancellation seemingly blocks just about as much background sound as my over-the-ear headphones. Equally great are both the transparency modes, which pump in outside sounds while you're wearing your AirPods, and Adaptive Transparency, which automatically adjusts the level of transparency based on how loud or soft your surroundings are. This is a great mode for wearing your AirPods in loud environments, so you can still hear everything without the noise becoming overwhelming. To that point, these AirPods are actually FDA-certified hearing aids.

Sources indicate that there are plenty of other features available here as well, especially if you have a compatible iPhone. AirPods Pro 3 have a built-in heart rate sensor, so you can track workouts without an Apple Watch; you can translate conversations in real time with Live Translate; "Conversation Awareness" lowers the volume of your audio and turns on transparency mode when you start speaking; and they run for eight hours on one charge with noise cancellation enabled.

Recent findings suggest that this isn't an in-depth list of the AirPods Pro 3's set of features. But suffice it to say, these earbuds are worth their full MSRP of $249. So not only can I wholeheartedly recommend them at $149, but I'd say they're an easy buy if you've been thinking about picking up AirPods for yourself.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: Veteran execs from the media, entertainment and brand sectors have teamed up to launch an all-purpose advisory coalition, we can reveal.

The Unlabelled Alliance comprises ex-UTA and Fremantle branded chief Sam Glynne, 7Wonder founder and TV producer Liza Abbott, Somethin’ Else director and audio industry veteran Steve Ackerman, Gleam Futures founder and creator economy talent manager Dom Smales and Little Dot Studios co-founder Selma Turajlic.

Each has more than 20 years’ experience in their field, and they will look to bring their particular expertise to the advisory, which will look at helping media companies transform, innovate and scale by unlocking the value of their IP and forming partnerships with other players in digital, audio, talent and the brand space. Related Stories Agencies Made By All Hires Ex-Spotter & Rolling Stone Exec Christina Tom News Endemol Shine Brasil & Grupo Podpah Set Digital Partnership Led By 'Temptation Island'.

According to recent reports, this will include monetizing content; repurposing catalog, licenses and distribution models; digital strategy; how to turn brands into partners, not simply sponsors; working with creators and talent; and backing the right digital-first ideas. Watch on Deadline.

Each member of the Unlabelled Alliance will continue to run their own businesses and ventures, and provide tailored advice and support to clients – meaning they can form different combinations and find solutions based on the firm.

The coalition is targeting broadcasters, studios, distributors, publishers, music companies, talent agencies, production companies and brands, and is pitching its offer as “experience-based solutions without the burden of fixed overheads.” As such they’re presenting the advisory as a “deliberately lean, plug-in model” that engages only as long as a problem requires.

Their rationale for the alliance is that the industry is not simply changing, but “fracturing and rebuilding itself in a completely different shape.” They note that broadcaster commission budgets are shrinking in many cases, while the creator economy is growing and formats often shift across mediums and platforms. The initiative for the business has been in the works for some time, with a website now up and running, and we understand several deals are set to conclude.

“We came together as a group, first as friends and then with a shared vision of using our experience to future-proof the industry that we’ve grown up in,” the Unlabelled Alliance co-founders said in a statement.

“We built our careers in traditional media and went on to revolutionise it from the inside out: building and scaling businesses, pioneering digital-first content, creating latest models for talent and re-imagining legacy IP potential. We know the pain points because we’ve been there. Our aim is your innovation and growth.”.

They added they would be a “hands-on and results-driven advisory team of seasoned specialists, helping C-suites, boards, founders and investors work out what is stopping them scaling and delivering real, smart and swift solutions.”.

Sources indicate that abbott will provide IP, studios and transformational and operational infrastructure advice. She was most recently the Chief Content Officer at The Earthshot Prize, Prince William’s environmental initiative. Prior to that, she was COO of Unscripted at Fremantle, overseeing Thames, Talkback, Boundless and Shotglass. She was co-founder of 7Wonder, the UK production joint venture of Maverick Television and Australia’s Seven Network that’s now part of Banijay. Abbott has also held senior roles at Maverick, ITV Studios, IMG and the BBC.

Ackerman intends to offer audio, podcasting and content strategy advice. He is known as one of radio giant and multimedia production pioneer Somethin’ Else’s early directors, and led the tech giant up to its sale to Sony Music Entertainment, at which point he became EVP and Head of Global Podcasts for the Sony. He is now a non-exec director of The Podcast Show and subscription platform SupaPass.

Glynne is the branded entertainment and IP strategy expert. She founded and was head of UTA’s EMEA Entertainment and Culture Marketing business, and worked as Global SVP of Branded Entertainment at Fremantle, working across 30 territories. Prior to that, she ran Renault TV and set up and ran The Audi Channel for All3Media and BBH. She’s also a Cannes Lions judge.

Smales, considered by many the architect of the creator economy and influencer world in Europe, will focus on talent and the creator economy solutions. He’s known for leading Gleam Futures, the early digital-first talent management business he founded in 2010. In 2021, he exited for Dentsu and now runs WinnieWood, a creator economy group that spans talent management, entertainment IP, commerce, tech and investments, and is a co-founder of creator-led entertainment producer GloMotion Studios.

Turajlic will handle digital transformation and entrepreneurship. She is known as co-founder of Little Dot Studios alongside the late Andy Taylor. The business, which now has well over 500 staff, has been singled out as a key pillar in growth for Banijay, which added Little Dot to its ranks through its acquisition of All3 this year. Turajlic also had senior roles at All3, Sony Pictures Television an Celador International, and is now a venture builder and angel investor with Alma Angels.

Breaking: Why Black Friday Is the Perfect Time to Start a Gym Membership

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most people are probably waiting until Jan.
  • The week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit.
  • This week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a latest air fryer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most people are probably waiting until Jan. 1 to start getting in shape, whether they want to start fresh or absolve themselves of their perceived holiday indulgences. Every year, people start the newly introduced year by joining a gym crowded with others newly resolved to get in shape, paying full price for the privilege of waiting in a long line to use the squat rack. This year, try something different: Start your gym membership during Black Friday.

The week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit. While you're comparing deals on latest tech, headphones, or smart home devices, here’s why you should also take a few minutes to scout out the gyms near you.

This week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a latest air fryer. Here are just a few examples of the offers out there right now:.

Orangetheory and F45 have various free-month and prize-entry promotions for newly introduced Black Friday sign-ups, and similar studios for Pilates, yoga, and strength training have discounted multi-month and annual packages.

Independent gyms, university rec centers, and local studios often run their own versions, from a free month tacked onto a longer commitment to waived joining fees.

Deals vary a lot by location, so call or stop by the clubs near you and ask what's available. Then remember to always read the fine print before you sign:.

Look at the price after the promotion ends, not just the first month's rate.

Ask about fees, including joining, annual, and access fees.

Try before you buy. Many gyms offer a free trial pass. It might make sense to first visit at the time of day you'd actually go.

Be honest about distance. The best gym is the one you'll actually walk into, so pick one that's close to home or work.

Gyms also run sales around Latest Year's, so a good Black Friday offer isn't the only deal you'll see. Even still, the savings aren't the only reason to go now.

December is reliably the quietest stretch of the gym year: People are busy with holiday travel and work deadlines, and many tell themselves they'll "start fresh in January." That means open benches, free treadmills, and staff who have time to show you how a machine works.

In a recent development, that's a gift for any gym-goer, but especially if you're latest. Learning your way around a gym is much less intimidating when it's empty. You can figure out the equipment, make your mistakes in peace, and build a routine before the January crowds arrive. Plus, this time of year is a perfect window to set and achieve a winnable goal.

From Black Friday to Latest Year's Day is about five weeks. By the time the January rush hits its peak and settles into its usual patterns, you could be eight weeks into a new routine. And as my colleague Beth Skwarecki explains, you really can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Beginners tend to see the fastest gains of their lifting lives in the first couple of months.

Recent findings suggest that prefer running? I know I do, and luckily, a couch-to-5K plan works the same way. Most programs run about nine weeks and build you up gradually from short run-walk intervals. Start the week after Black Friday and you'll be running for a solid stretch by early January, and you'll be well on your way to 30 minutes at a stretch by the end of the month. By the time your New Year's resolution friends are just starting, you'll already be a few runs in.

According to recent reports, this is also the season when many workplaces and health looks wrap up their open enrollment periods, which makes it a smart time to check what wellness perks you already have. Before you pay full price for anything, look into:.

Workplace wellness programs, which sometimes offer gym reimbursements, discounted memberships or fitness stipends.

Health insurance perks, since some plans include gym memberships or discounts.

According to recent reports, HSA and FSA rules, where general gym memberships usually don't qualify, but some medically recommended programs may. Also check any year-end deadlines for money you'd otherwise lose.

Corporate and employer discounts, which many large gyms offer on top of regular promotions.

Stack a workplace benefit on top of a holiday sale, and your cost per workout can drop considerably—well before New Year's resolution time arrives.

#165613. Jevons Paradox in AI: Cheaper Tokens Won't Pay for Capex

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1194 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Philippdubach ↗ Open Full Page

Jevons Paradox in AI: Cheaper Tokens Won't Pay for Capex

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1194 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Philippdubach

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In March I wrote that the hyperscalers’ answer to collapsing inference prices is Jevons: cheaper tokens create so much demand that total spending grows anyway.
  • Google processed 9.7 trillion tokens a month in May 2024.
  • Revenue is price times volume, and the price is falling too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In March I wrote that the hyperscalers’ answer to collapsing inference prices is Jevons: cheaper tokens create so much demand that total spending grows anyway.

On volume, they look right. Google processed 9.7 trillion tokens a month in May 2024. In May 2026 it was 3.2 quadrillion, 330 times as many. Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle spent $230 billion on capex in the third quarter of 2026 alone, almost four times what they spent two years earlier.

But tokens aren’t dollars. Revenue is price times volume, and the price is falling too. So my question is: does demand for tokens grow faster than the price of a token collapses?

If the price of a token falls 10x and volume grows 10x, revenue is flat. Revenue only grows when volume grows faster than the price falls.

Google’s first-party model APIs went from 7 billion tokens a minute in Q3 2025 to nearly 32 billion in Q3 2026, up 4.6x. Google’s tokens across all products grew 6.7x between the I/O keynotes of 2025 and 2026. OpenRouter went from 0.5 trillion to 128 trillion tokens a week in 20 months, about 27x a year. On the price side, MIT researchers find that the price of reaching a fixed benchmark score falls 5 to 10x a year, and Epoch AI finds that cost per task at fixed performance falls about 13x a year.

According to recent reports, volume and price move at about the same speed. That proves nothing by itself, because Google’s tokens aren’t sold at fixed-capability prices (like the ones Epoch measures). But it lines up with what Mert Demirer, Andrey Fradkin, Nadav Tadelis and Sida Peng found when they used OpenRouter and Azure data to estimate short-run price elasticities “just above one” and concluded that this leaves “limited scope for Jevons-Paradox effects.” At an elasticity of one, a 10x price cut buys 10x the tokens for the same money.

That matches how a lot of buyers behave. Say a bank’s head of operations has $2 million approved for AI contract review, and then the vendor cuts its token prices tenfold. The bank can now review ten times as many contracts, which is great. The budget still indicates $2 million. To spend more, the head of operations would have to walk into the CFO’s office and argue that the product got cheaper and so deserves a bigger budget, and I wouldn’t want to make that case. So the bank spends the same $2 million. The vendor can say, truthfully, that token volume grew tenfold.

But I guess there’s also a counterargument. Cheaper tokens change what people build. When inference is nearly free, developers design agents that call a model hundreds of times per task, and a recent theory paper argues this can make demand rise faster than prices fall. That may happen.

Recent findings suggest that “The price of a token” hides two curves that move in opposite directions. (1) The price of a fixed level of capability is falling. GPT-4-level answers cost a small fraction of what they did in 2023, and the decline continues. (2) The cost of using the best model available is rising. The same MIT paper finds that the cost of running frontier models on benchmarks rises 3 to 18x a year, because each generation is larger and reasons for longer.

Industry observers note that A concrete case: to run the Artificial Analysis benchmark suite, Claude Opus 5.5 at maximum effort used 218 million output tokens, almost three times the median model, at about $10 per task. At low effort the same model used about a tenth of the tokens.

In a recent development, spending probably follows the frontier curve (at least up until now). In enterprises, open-weight models now handle 19% of tokens but get 4% of spend, while frontier labs take 69% of deployment dollars. Cheap tokens and expensive tokens are close to two separate markets (the cheap one grows fast in volume and barely registers in revenue).

It has been revealed that I don’t want to wave the demand away. Google’s token count is the clearest public series we have, and it’s steep.

Sources indicate that agents account for much of it. A paper by Bai, Brynjolfsson, Pentland and co-authors finds that agentic coding tasks use about 1,000 times more tokens than chat about the same code. Anthropic reported in 2025 that multi-agent systems use about 15 times more tokens than chat. OpenRouter dates February 6, 2026 as the last day humans used more tokens on its platform than agents did.

If cheaper tokens alone don’t grow revenue, the money has to come from somewhere else. Bain estimates AI needs $2 trillion of annual revenue by 2030 to fund the compute being built, and that it will still be $800 billion short even if companies reinvest every dollar AI saves them in sales, marketing, support and R&D.

You can already see vendors reaching for that money in their pricing. Intercom charges $0.99 for each customer case its Fin agent resolves, a price set against the cost of a support agent’s time, whatever the tokens cost. Salesforce has changed its Agentforce pricing three times since 2024. The direction is clear. Vendors want to be paid per outcome, and an outcome is priced against a (human) wage.

Workers aged 22 to 25 in the jobs most exposed to AI saw a 13% relative drop in employment compared with less exposed peers. US employers cited AI in about 121,000 revealed job cuts in the first ten months of 2026, about a fifth of all announced cuts.

Spending grew faster than I expected when I wrote in March. Back then the five companies guided to $660 to $690 billion for 2026. Their SEC filings show $560 billion of cash capex in the first three quarters, with $230 billion in Q3 alone. That excludes finance leases, so the full figure is higher.

Sources indicate that the cash flow squeeze I described has arrived. Oracle spent 174% of its operating cash flow on capex in its fiscal 2026 and Amazon 94% in 2025. Microsoft is at 63%, Meta at 60% and Alphabet at 56%, all well above where they were a few years ago.

It has been revealed that so far the clearest winner is the company selling the equipment. Nvidia reported $116 billion of revenue at a 75% gross margin in its latest quarter, and its revenue has grown in step with hyperscaler capex for three years.

Sources indicate that the model labs sit lower. Press reports put OpenAI’s gross margin at 33 to 39%, depending on the quarter. Anthropic’s S-1 shows about an 85% gross margin, but it books training compute under R&D, so the figure only measures the cost of serving existing models. Even so, it suggests the cost of serving tokens may be falling faster than their price.

Markets have priced the split. Since ChatGPT launched, the semiconductor index has roughly tripled while software stocks and the S&P 500 are both up about 70%. Chips have also fallen 41% from their June peak, so the market is less sure than it was in the summer.

Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (829 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, said last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

It has been revealed that in fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

Industry observers note that the law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.

12 Things to Do on Christmas If You Don’t Celebrate

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it.
  • According to recent reports, you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex.
  • In a recent development, if Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in a way, the Christmas season is more fun if you don’t celebrate it. You get to enjoy all the brightly colored lights your neighbors put up, but you don’t have to put up your own. You don’t have to do any duty-shopping. There's no pressure. But Christmas Day itself leaves you in a mostly shuttered world that feels like there’s nothing going on. Fortunately, there are options to make Dec. 25 a fun day off, regardless of your observances.

According to recent reports, you can’t go wrong with some moo shu pork and a trip to the multiplex. Chinese restaurants and movie theaters traditionally stay open on Christmas Day for those who don't celebrate, and they’re often filled with fellow Christmas refugees. Check Google for the hours of your local Chinese restaurant and give them a call to make a reservation. If you’re more adventurous and you’re in a city large enough to have a Chinatown (or a whatever-town), just head straight there on Christmas and see what happens—that’s how the best days usually start.

In a recent development, if Chinese food isn’t your thing, look at restaurants serving any non-European cuisine—Greek places, Japanese places, and Mediterranean places are usually open, as are plenty of Italian restaurants and steakhouses. Just make sure you check first. Lots of chain restaurants are open on Christmas Day too, including Applebee's, McDonald’s, Benihana, and more. You can even get Christmas breakfast at your local IHOP. But not every location of every outlet follows the same hours.

As for movies, most chain multiplex theaters are open on Dec. 25, and theaters are usually pretty full. The movies attract both people who don't celebrate Christmas and people who do, but want to get away from their families for a couple hours, so make sure and reserve a seat beforehand. Consider hitting up an out-of-the-way spot or that theater with the table service and cushy recliners to make it feel like more of an occasion.

Most people going to the movies on Christmas Day aren’t there for Christmas movies, so interesting “secular” movies are often slated for release on the 25th. This year's Christmas is unusually packed with interesting upcoming movies, including family flick Jumani: Open World, a Robert Eggers horror movie called Werwulf, and the crowd pleasing football story Mr. Irrelevant, so you have serious options.

Chinese restaurants and movie theaters aren’t the only establishments open on Christmas. Here are some other options:.

According to recent reports, go skiing or snowboarding: Most mountains are open on Christmas, and the lift lines are blissfully empty. There's no better way of celebrating a winter-based holiday than on a wide-open mountain.

Visit a skating rink: Speaking of winter sports, ice skating rinks are generally open on Christmas too.

In a recent development, pretend to be a tourist: Tourist attractions are often open on Christmas, especially in larger cities. This includes places like Madame Tussaud’s and Ripley’s Believe It or Not, as well as ziplines and Segway tours—so do that touristy thing you’ve never done before.

Get a room: If you’ve got some spare cash and have nothing better to do, get a room at a hotel. Hotels don’t usually close on Christmas, and they typically offer plenty of amenities, so take advantage of the pool at the Holiday Inn or the spa at the Four Seasons, depending on your lifestyle.

Hiking and biking: Hiking trails and parks are open on Christmas if you want to get outdoors. If you’re into biking, hit the trails or hit the streets: Traffic is minimal on Christmas, so it’s a great time to put in some serious roadwork.

In a recent development, volunteer: Not having anything to do on Christmas isn’t the biggest life problem, especially compared to people who have nowhere to go and nothing to eat. So use Christmas to help people and actually deliver on that whole “good will towards men” thing. Check your local Craigslist for volunteering opportunities.

Use Christmas as a catch-up day: This is strictly for type-A people, but if everyone is out of town and no one is going to call you, why not spend the day catching up on neglected chores or personal projects? You can spend at least part of your day knocking a few things off your to-do list and the rest of the time relaxing. That way you’ll get a break and still feel accomplished.

Just sleep all day: Type-B personalities like me see a day free of obligations and other people as a golden opportunity to do as little as is humanly possible, a day to fully commit to sloth.

Spend time with friends and family at home: Not celebrating Christmas doesn’t mean you can’t spend the day with family and/or friends. Get together with your loved ones, play games, watch a movie, cook together, talk, or whatever else you all enjoy. You don’t have to go out to have fun, so don’t rule out staying in with people you care about.

In a recent development, shopping: This is at the bottom of the list because it’s iffy. Drug stores and convenience stores like 711 are usually open on the 25th. Grocery chains like Kroger’s and Trader Joe’s usually aren’t. Your local shopping mall or retail district might be open, but probably won't be, so check ahead.

Because so many places are closed on Christmas Day, you should plan ahead (unless you like spontaneity and are OK with the possibility of disappointment) by:.

Making a list of the places you want to go.

Calling nearby locations to confirm they’ll be open, as not every chain follows corporate holiday hour recommendations.

Making reservations at any restaurant(s) you initiative to visit.

Putting together a basic timeline of the day, accounting for travel time, so you don’t lose any reservations, miss a movie, or arrive after the store closes.

The most crucial advice here is to do something intentional on Christmas, even if it's sleeping in, so the day doesn't feel depressing or empty. So hit the slopes, suck down some dim sum, or keep your couch from floating away, but be sure you make Christmas your own.

Whether you’re looking for an affordable robot vacuum for a small apartment or the ultimate flagship model capable of coping with the challenges of a large home, pet hair, and more, there’s a Roborock model for you – and with Black Friday savings of up to $1,650, there’s never been a better time to buy.

Roborock’s 2026 flagship model offers the ultimate in truly intelligent cleaning thanks to a combination of raw cleaning power and a market-leading combination of smart features.

The benefits begin with a combination of raw power, reach, and fully automated self-cleaning. The Saros 20 delivers 36,000 Pa suction power with a dual anti-tangle system, ensuring no hassle with even the toughest of pet hairs, while a FlexiArm system ensures true edge-to-edge cleaning. The fully automated dock takes care of emptying the dust as well as washing and drying the mops.

AdaptiLift Chassis 3.0 enables the Saros 20 to move freely around the most largest and most complex of homes. A combination of an advanced vision system, adaptive algorithms, and a mechanical system comprising a main wheel, auxiliary wheel, and climbing arm mean that the device can cope with most thresholds between rooms. This even includes double layer thresholds, totaling 3.46 inches.

It has been revealed that the Saros 20 uses StarSight Autonomous System 2.0, an industry-first navigation system with true 3D mapping of your home. The setup combines LiDAR with time-of-flight measurements to create an accurate depth map with both visual and infrared camera systems. The specs are unrivaled, with a sampling frequency more than 20 times higher than other devices and 21,600 sensor points, but what counts are the results. The AI powered system can recognize more than 300+ types of obstacles, even when they are are less than an inch in width and height. That means it can avoid anything from a loose cable to an inquisitive pet.

AdaptiLift technology combines with a Carpet Intelligence System to enables the Saros 20 to detect when it is moving from solid flooring to carpet. At the most basic level, this means the mops will never get your carpets wet, but the system is far more sophisticated than this. The robot will automatically lift itself up onto deep pile carpets before lowering to the optimal height for vacuuming. It can cope with carpets with a pile height of 1.18 inches.

Finally, Smart Blueprint 3.0 is the AI-powered intelligent cleaning system that analyzes your home’s unique layout, floor materials, and the behavior patterns of everyone in the home in order to automatically optimise its cleaning routines. You also get voice and app control and can even check on your pets while away by asking the Saros 20 to locate them and provide a live video feed.

Other film and TV links evident in the selection include author and illustrator Shaun Tan, who co-directed the Oscar-winning animated short ‘The Lost Thing’.

Sources indicate that colfer is shortlisted for ‘War’, a graphic novel he co-wrote with Andrew Donkin and which is illustrated by Giovanni Rigano. Sources indicate that the eight-strong shortlist of titles for kids aged 8 to 12 comprises five novels, two graphic novels and an illustrated collection of short stories. Watch on Deadline.

Sources indicate that stars including Adeel Akhtar (Enola Holmes), Dafne Keen (His Dark Materials) and Aidan Turner (Poldark) will read from the shortlisted titles in a series of short films showcasing the books. The films for the grown-up Booker have amassed millions of views.

The judging panel overseeing the process includes Ghosts star Lolly Adefope and bookseller Sanchita Basu De Sarkar, as well as Frank Cottrell-Boyce, a writer and screenwriter whose film credits include Paddington in Peru and Kensuke’s Kingdom. They are joined by four child judges. The inaugural Children’s Booker winner will be confirmed at a daytime ceremony at the Young V&A Museum in London on Feb. 2, 2027.

The main Booker Prize is regarded as the single biggest accolade in the world for a work of literary fiction. The film and TV links are evident in the scores of Booker titles that have been adapted for the screen including Hilary Mantel’s ‘Wolf Hall’ and Thomas Keneally’s ‘Schindler’s Ark’ (published as ‘Schindler’s List’ in the U.S.).

The 2025 winner David Szalay told Deadline about a film adaptation of his Booker-winning novel ‘Flesh’ from the producers of Conclave. This year’s winner, M. John Harrison, also told us about his hopes for a film adaptation of The End of Everything.

Here’s the Children’s Booker Prize shortlist in full.

‘The Worst Thing That Could Possibly Happen’ by Guy Bass, illustrated by David Roberts (Little Tiger Press).

‘Tadpole Summer’ by Catherine Bruton (Nosy Crow).

‘War’ by Eoin Colfer and Andrew Donkin, illustrated by Giovanni Rigano (Hodder Children’s Books).

‘The Night I Borrowed Time’ by Iqbal Hussain (Puffin Press).

‘The Teller of Tall Tales’ by Liz Hyder, illustrated by Tom de Freston (Pushkin Children’s Books).

‘The Rambler’s Curse’ by Mikey Please (HarperCollins Children’s Books).

‘Séamus Almost Famous’ by Jessica Scott-Whyte, illustrated by Becka Moor (Gill Children’s).

‘Hometown’ by Shaun Tan (Walker Studio).

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

EXCLUSIVE: As the controversial use of non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) rears its head once again in the UK entertainment industry, the head of Channel 4 News has told staff her division no longer engages in the practice.

Deadline understands Esme Wren sent an all-staffer on Saturday after the issue of Channel 4 News using NDAs was raised on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme.

Introducing the topic, Today host Nick Robinson stated: “Channel 4 News indicates they don’t use NDAs, well only for commercial matters, but others suggest they do and it’s difficult for people to get to the bottom of the truth in those cases where the nature of things makes it difficult to talk about.” Related Stories News Susan Sarandon Joins Natalie Dormer, Richard Armitage & Susan Wokoma In Signing Open Letter Calling For Entertainment Industry To "Acknowledge Role It Plays" In Enabling Bad Behavior News Russell Brand's Wife Promises Not To Pass On Further Prison Messages.

Wren reacted to Robinson’s remarks by emailing staff and inviting questions during yesterday’s morning news meeting, we are told. Watch on Deadline.

Wren’s email, which Deadline has obtained passages from, said ITN “stopped using confidentiality clauses, which prevent people speaking freely about their time at ITN, over three years ago,” while “in a small number of cases where they were used in the past they have been lifted for both former and current employees.” She also stressed that ITN has “listened and apologised for things got wrong in the past.”.

ITN apologized unreservedly to those affected by NDA use after an independent review in 2024 found in a small number of historic cases, the use of confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements had been applied inconsistently or lacked clarity.

That review tasked ITN, which also makes news for ITV and Skydance UK network 5, with reviewing its use of NDAs and improving whistleblowing processes following allegations that it used NDAs to cover up gender pay discrimination, harassment and bullying. In a leaked recording obtained by Deadline from an ITN town hall a few weeks after the review came out, lead Channel 4 News anchor Krishnan Guru-Murthy criticized Channel 4 News’ management over the problem . This came after high-profile cases of ITN using NDAs were raised in parliament by British lawmakers.

An ITN spokeswoman mentioned: “ITN does not use NDAs to prevent people talking openly about their experiences with the manufacturer, including at Channel 4 News. We stopped using confidentiality clauses in settlement agreements in 2022, and also lifted them from the small number of people who had previously been subject to them. We have listened and learned, and apologised where we have got things wrong in the past.”.

Discussion about NDAs has returned to the fore in UK entertainment after Russell Brand was sentence to 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assault and allegations about David Walliams were published by The Guardian and ITN-operated ITV News, allegations that Walliams vehemently denies. Both celebrities were reported to have used NDAs, prompting British ministers to look into ways they can rapidly change the law to expand protections that stop NDAs being used to cover up harassment or discrimination. These protections are being implemented via the upcoming Employment Rights Act.

The UK’s influential Digital, Culture, Media & Sport Committee has annonced a high-profile probe into industry NDA use, with evidence sessions set to begin in two weeks. Witnesses and timings will be announced shortly and it feels highly likely that executives from ITN or Channel 4 will be invited to speak. Separately, Channel 4, where Brand used to host demonstrates, has been under pressure for historic NDA use, with CEO Priya Dogra telling the committee last week that the network uses confidentality clauses in a limited way with “pretty large caveats.” One lawmaker referenced Deadline’s exclusive report from last year that found Channel 4 had paid out nearly £5M ($6.5M) to ex-employees who signed settlement deals to prevent complaints escalating, but in doing so, stipulated that they do not discuss matters relating to the manufacturer.

10 Hidden Controls Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests.
  • In a recent development, if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.
  • Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely new side of the game.

In a recent development, if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

According to recent reports, EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

If you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

Sources indicate that when you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

Industry observers note that while driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

Stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

Sources indicate that when you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

In a recent development, ice storms cause long outages because several exposures act together. Ice adds weight to conductors, hardware and structures. Wind pushes on the larger iced surface. Trees and limbs bend into the line and add impact and uneven load. Conductors may also gallop and lose clearance. This paper explains how these loads combine and why the complete line must be assessed, not a single component. It reviews a monitored winter test of three conductor systems. It also summarizes utility records from a major regional ice storm. Finally, it outlines how to choose corridors, blueprint restoration and keep crews and the public safe around covered conductors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of people. Here are the details.

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that latest job listings on Apple’s website indicate the company’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the company has also introduced fresh restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple revealed prepares to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give users more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

Over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “strategy and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

Recent findings suggest that today’s report on the latest job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring consumers to initiate every step. With the new job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its looks for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how promptly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally launched its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.
