📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that after releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the company is now rolling out the public beta for users looking to try the latest features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming.

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with upcoming privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

Those came alongside several new features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

And speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing consumers to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing latest tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful patch, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and users on the public beta can now try out these newly introduced features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

I didn’t know what to expect from this 1937 video explanation of how wire photos were transmitted to newspapers, but a double stunt sequence featuring an airplane and a death-defying photographer was not anywhere on my bingo card. This starts kinda slow but it picks up once they get into the completely fascinating explanation of how they sent photographs across the country using ordinary telephone lines. The whole setup was portable and they just hacked into a wire on a telephone pole, asked the operator to clear the line, and sent a photo scan via an analog modem. Ingenious!

The Wikipedia page about wire photos is worth a read — French designers argued that the technology was responsible for an early form of fast fashion.

Industry observers note that sort by: thread — thread . latest . faves.

According to recent reports, hi, journalist here, this wild technology was still in use into the early 90s at least. I remember working at a little paper in South Carolina when AP rolled out an early way to see photos on a computer screen instead of waiting for the wacky old spinning drum machines to spit out prints, one by one, that you'd physically thumb through. It felt like magic. But truth be told, the spinning drum thing was also magic.

You can read more about wire photos on Tedium: Pushing Photos Through Wires.

According to recent reports, premium customers get up to 15 free minutes a month, Metal customers up to 20, and Ultra up to 30, on either an e-scooter or an e-bike. The unlock fee is waived as well, as students get a 10-minute ride, available in the Netherlands, Italy, and Spain for now.

“After the integration of Revolut Pay into Dott’s payment checkout last year, partnering further with Revolut allows us to bring clean, convenient transport solutions directly to millions of active customers, in a very seamless way” noted Matthieu Faure, VP Brand, Comms & Global Partnerships of Dott.

“By integrating Dott benefits straight into the Revolut app, we are making sustainable urban travel even more rewarding and accessible across key European cities.”.

It has been revealed that dott became the largest operator of its kind in Europe through the TIER-Dott merger, completed in March 2024. It now runs 200,000 shared vehicles across 400 cities in Europe and the Middle East, and notes its 12 million users have taken more than 500 million rides so far.

Putting its vehicles inside bigger consumer apps has become a habit for Dott. A similar deal in April put free monthly rides inside Wolt’s subscription scheme in eight countries, and Dott vehicles already appear in the FREE NOW and Citymapper apps.

In a recent development, the draw for Dott is Revolut’s reach: more than 80 million customers, who make over a billion transactions a month between them. The fintech also remains Europe’s most valuable private tech tech giant.

You can spend plenty of time getting your Mac, display, and desk just right. But what about the chair you use every day? Between typing, taking video calls, and leaning back to watch something, your position changes throughout the day. Your chair should be able to keep up.

That’s the idea behind LiberNovo’s ergonomic chairs, which combine support that moves with you and a choice of sizes, including the Maxis range for bigger and taller users. For Black Friday, LiberNovo is taking up to 42% off in the U.S., with chairs starting at $609 and offers running November 19–30.

Sources indicate that adjusting a chair for your desk is one thing. Keeping that support as you change position is another. LiberNovo’s Dynamic Support System links the neck support, backrest, armrests, and seat so they move together as you recline.

It has been revealed that the Bionic FlexFit Backrest adds eight flexible panels that contour independently. Rather than relying on a single rigid backrest, the design lets different sections follow your back as you shift or turn. Once you’ve adjusted the chair to fit, the system is designed to maintain contact through those movements with fewer manual readjustments.

In a recent development, both the Omni and Maxis families offer five recline positions: 105, 115, 125, 135, and 160 degrees. That gives you options for desk work, a more relaxed position for watching a video, and a deeper recline for a break.

A higher weight limit is only part of finding a chair that fits. Taller users also need enough seat depth, a headrest that reaches the right spot, and armrests with room to adjust.

Recent findings suggest that the LiberNovo Maxis range addresses those details with a 52 cm seat depth, a wider backrest with a flared base, and an extended-travel headrest with 140 mm of vertical adjustment and 120 mm of front-to-back adjustment. Its armrests sit lower and offer a wider, longer adjustment range to accommodate larger builds.

LiberNovo recommends Maxis for users approximately 5 feet 10 inches to 6 feet 7 inches tall, with a maximum supported weight of 399 pounds. Maxis is certified to BIFMA X5.11. The seat cushion uses firmer support at the rear and a softer front edge, while a six-spring Controlled Recline System is designed to build resistance progressively as you lean back.

For a shallower seat, the Omni family offers 45 cm and 48 cm configurations. Choosing between the two families starts with fit, then comes down to which features you want.

There are three feature tiers in each family. Omni SE and Maxis Manual offer manually adjusted lumbar support, without a motor or battery. Both retain the flexible backrest, dynamic support, and five recline positions.

The Maxis Electric includes motorized lumbar adjustment and OmniStretch, a five-minute powered stretch sequence used in deep recline.

Omni Pro and Maxis Airflow add Active AirFlow seat ventilation. A fan draws air through the cushion to carry heat away, and an occupancy sensor pauses the fan when you stand up. These models also include a larger 3,000 mAh rechargeable battery.

LiberNovo’s warranty covers the frame and structural components for six years, and electronic components for two years.

Industry observers note that bundles add another option. The Omni Pro Standard Bundle includes the chair and a footrest for $983. The Maxis Electric Premium Bundle includes the chair, a footrest, and an extra battery for $1,202, down from a listed MSRP of $2,086.

Sources indicate that liberNovo is also offering 30-day price protection on eligible purchases. U.S. gift tiers begin at $800 for a Mouse Pad, $1,000 for an Eco-Comfort three-piece gift set, and $1,200 for an Ergo-to-Go Travel Suite. In a recent development, whatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the latest limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

WhatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the fresh limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the enhancement becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

Sources indicate that this rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the firm confirmed four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

Liverpool are ready to let a long-serving stalwart leave Anfield for free in 2027, according to one insider.

The last player standing from the tail end of Brendan Rodgers’ managerial reign, Joe Gomez is now into his 12th season with the Reds, albeit that he’s been consigned to a backup role thus far under Andoni Iraola.

The 29-year-old has featured for just 259 minutes across our 16 matches so far in this campaign, more than half of which have come in the Carabao Cup (Transfermarkt), and as it stand he’ll be out of contract in seven months’ time.

Ex-Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown has claimed that Liverpool sporting director Julian Ward has already decided that the club’s longest-serving current player won’t be offered a upcoming deal, with injury challenges not helping the defender’s case.

According to recent reports, he told Football Insider: “Liverpool have already decided they’re going to let Joe Gomez leave. He doesn’t have much of a role to play at the moment, he’s not starting games at right-back even despite their injuries, and he isn’t competing for a centre-back position.

Sources indicate that “His injuries are always a concern as well. They don’t think he can start games consistently, and all of these challenges stack up eventually.

“It would be a surprise to me if they were to offer him a new contract, especially when you consider they’re going to be looking to bring in new defenders at some stage.

“If he hasn’t played much this season, that’s not going to change with new players coming in, so I expect he’ll be allowed to look at what other options might be available.”.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Ward could be quite busy with contract renewals over the next few months, with Alisson Becker, Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister reportedly all in line for prospective new deals.

Whereas that trio are virtually guaranteed to start, though, Gomez usually has to rely on substitute appearances or heavy squad rotation for domestic cup games, and it’s not implausible that he could be allowed to depart on a free transfer next summer.

If that is indeed his fate, he’ll be assured of a raucous send-off at Anfield on the final day of the season, with his popularity among the fan base unmistakably evident by the roar which greeted his successful penalty in the Carabao Cup shootout triumph over Chelsea last month.

As Lewis Steele rightly said, the 29-year-old ‘very rarely puts a foot wrong’ whenever he’s called upon, and even if he isn’t getting much game-time, we don’t doubt that he’s imparting some invaluable advice to the young defenders at Liverpool who can learn so much from him.

Recent findings suggest that if this is to be Gomez’s last campaign with the Reds, all we ask is that he does finally, finally get his first goal for the club during regulation time. You’d be very hard pressed to find a more popular goalscorer if that moment were to happen!

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (431 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thenextweb

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The US Commerce Department has put Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud organization at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, on its trade blacklist, after officials and lawmakers spent weeks asking why it was taking so long.
  • Moreover, the Entity List filing also caught six firms seen as Megaspeed affiliates in Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.
  • I’ve led the push for the Department of Commerce to crack down on Megaspeed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The US Commerce Department has put Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud organization at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, on its trade blacklist, after officials and lawmakers spent weeks asking why it was taking so long.

Moreover, the Entity List filing also caught six firms seen as Megaspeed affiliates in Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand.

I’ve led the push for the Department of Commerce to crack down on Megaspeed. I’m glad it’s finally moving forward.

According to recent reports, the Department of Commerce still needs to explain to Congress why this took so long. Other agencies including the Departments of State, Treasury, and War supported the designation.

— Senator Pete Ricketts (@SenatorRicketts) November 23, 2026.

A place on the list means US firms need a licence to sell it goods, software, or tech, and such requests are usually refused. Listed firms also struggle to get spare parts and updates for gear they already run.

US investigators have spent more than a year looking into whether Megaspeed, long one of Nvidia’s bigger customers, funnelled advanced chips into China, where export rules bar their sale. The Justice Department has opened a criminal inquiry, and Nvidia says it chose to stop selling to the firm in June 2025.

In a recent development, why the listing took so long had become a sore point at the top of the US government. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about it at a White House meeting this month, Axios reported, though Commerce states that never happened.

Four departments had wanted Megaspeed listed for months, but “commerce has the pen,” Bessent told CNBC this month.

The scandal runs through the tech giant’s former boss, Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang. US spy agencies reportedly came to suspect her of working for Chinese intelligence, a claim that was not confirmed until now.

Nvidia investigates after CEO admits affair linked to spy reports.

Industry observers note that jensen Huang resigned as CEO on 11 November, after 33 years running the firm he co-founded. On the same day Megaspeed was blacklisted, Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to reinstate him.

Recent findings suggest that megaspeed denies doing anything wrong and notes Alice Huang left the firm in August 2025. The rule took effect on Monday, when it was filed for public inspection, and formal publication in the Federal Register follows on Wednesday.

Industry News: Freeing the iPod Nano 5G

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1572 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viktorkrapivin

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A few years ago, CUB3D demonstrated unsigned code execution on the iPod nano 6G and 7G through ipod_sun, a font-based exploit.
  • I wanted to get Rockbox running on the nano 5G, so I set out to adapt the exploit.
  • Existing DFU exploits, including q3kâs wInd3x, provide code execution on the nano 5G, but booting custom code this way requires a computer each time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A few years ago, CUB3D demonstrated unsigned code execution on the iPod nano 6G and 7G through ipod_sun, a font-based exploit. Whether the same approach would work on the 5G was still an open question.

I wanted to get Rockbox running on the nano 5G, so I set out to adapt the exploit. My motivation was simple: an up-to-date music player without an internet connection. I built a fully untethered boot chain that loads Rockbox from the nano 5Gâs NAND, with no computer or button sequence needed after installation. I also found a way to make the existing exploit fully untethered on the nano 7G, and likely the 6G too.

Existing DFU exploits, including q3kâs wInd3x, provide code execution on the nano 5G, but booting custom code this way requires a computer each time. I used wInd3x to explore the device and develop a convenient, fully untethered exploit. The firmware details below refer to the latest nano 5G firmware, 1.0.2 (34A20020).

It has been revealed that the nano 5Gâs NAND flash appears through a flash translation layer (FTL) as a logical disk with 4 KiB sectors. Its partition table separates a small private area for persistent device state, a firmware partition containing boot programs and resources, and a data volume for user files. The firmware partition has a directory of named images; the fonts live inside rsrc, a resource volume formatted as FAT16.

In a recent development, the original ipod_sun chain combines a resource-validation bypass with a font-parser vulnerability. Appleâs firmware directory identifies the normal operating system as osos, the disk-mode program as disk, and the resource image containing fonts as rsrc. The disk-mode boot path does not request the resource signature check used by normal OS boot.

Swapping the disk and osos directory entries exploits that difference: selecting disk mode now introduces Appleâs regular OS under the disk-mode policy. The OS still reads its fonts, but the bootloader has not required a valid signature for the modified resource image.

Recent findings suggest that the font then triggers CVE-2010-1797, the FreeType CFF stack-overflow vulnerability also known through the star exploit. A malformed font program corrupts the parserâs stack and redirects execution. My 5G port adapts that technique to the deviceâs font and execution context.

The swapped images remain on disk, but each restart still requires choosing disk mode with the deviceâs buttons. A normal boot selects the other entry. I wanted a better experience, with the modified font loading through the normal OS path.

In a recent development, the bootloader is organized into EFI-style modules stored as Portable Executable (PE) images. The module that passes execution to the next boot stage decides whether to validate rsrc. It first asks the PrivateData module for FirmwareStatus, which comes from an authenticated record in the private NAND partition.

The decisive branch is below. This is reconstructed C from the reverse-engineered routine, with unrelated fuse handling and protocol setup omitted.

According to recent reports, A value of 2 returns success before the resource-validation query. Bit 0 must remain clear: it is checked first, so 3 would reject the boot attempt. Tracing the restore OS reveals that it sets the status to 1 during firmware transfer and clears it to 0 at the end. This suggests an enhancement-in-progress guard that prevents booting an incomplete installation.

Sources indicate that appleâs resource-mount path writes status 2 only on the first successful boot, after rsrc has passed signature verification. My hypothesis is that this avoids repeating signature verification to shorten boot time or reduce energy use.

In a recent development, this is the second bypass. Instead of disguising the normal OS as disk mode, I can leave the firmware directory alone and supply a valid private record with bit 1 set. The normal boot path then accepts the modified resource image, and its font delivers code execution automatically.

The record lives in the private partition, identified by MBR type 0x3e. On the 5G layout I examined, the partition begins at logical block 1, with 4 KiB blocks. The bootloader reads a 512-byte header from its start. The status-bearing format begins with the little-endian magic PRVD and has this layout:.

The integrity tag is device-specific, so creating and saving a valid PRVD record requires code execution on that iPod.

Industry observers note that the tag is the first 16 bytes of the SHA-1 digest, encrypted with the deviceâs hardware AES UID key, selected through key slot 2. It authenticates the private header, but as the authentication is constructed on device we can falsify it if we have code execution.

To inspect and upgrade the private partition, I adapted emCORE, an older framework from freemyipodâs earlier iPod exploitation and boot work. It provided an existing USB-controlled environment to extend for the 5G.

In a recent development, I wrote the nano 5G NAND driver and integrated it into emCORE alongside the flash translation layer (FTL) and hardware AES access. Iâll cover the flash memory sequencer subsystem (FMSS), which enables NAND writes, in a future post. The FTL presents logical sectors over physical flash; it is the layer through which I read and write the private record and install the modified font.

Industry observers note that the private-status tool verifies the existing header and tag, constructs the updated record, and obtains its new tag from the device. It rechecks the partition table and header before writing, then flushes the write and reads it back. The tool writes a complete 4 KiB logical sector even though the bootloader only consumes the smaller header. This works on nano 5G hardware.

Industry observers note that once the private record and modified font are installed, they remain in NAND across restarts. emCORE and the host computer are needed for the installation workflow, not for each subsequent boot.

It has been revealed that reaching the font parser automatically solved persistence. The next constraint was fitting something useful inside the font. I wanted it to load Rockbox from storage, so the payload needed a NAND driver, a flash translation layer, a filesystem reader, and enough startup code to hand off reliably.

Industry observers note that to fit, I compiled with size and link-time optimizations and had the linker remove unused sections. The Rockbox kernel is stored on the deviceâs FAT32 partition and can be easily updated.

It has been revealed that code execution initially arrives in a damaged FreeType call frame. The stack has been corrupted, and Appleâs OS has left interrupts, DMA controllers, timers, caches, and address translation configured for its own use. Jumping straight into a large C program would carry that state into storage initialization.

Recent findings suggest that I split the bootstrap into two images. The first is the 808-byte assembly stub at 0x22050000. Its job is to leave the parser context: mask IRQs and FIQs, switch to a private stack, stop inherited timer activity, quiesce DMA and clock domains, and clean up caches and the MMU before entering the main payload. It replaces the damaged stack and then jumps to the Rockbox kernel loader.

Industry observers note that the second image is the main loader at 0x22060000. Its entry code disables the watchdog before starting the NAND scan, installs its own stack, and clears the uninitialized-data area before calling C. The watchdog matters because reconstructing the logical flash mapping can take several seconds; a reset in the middle would stop the boot before it ever found Rockbox.

This separation keeps the most fragile stage small. The assembly stub establishes a controlled execution environment; the main payload can then do the more substantial storage work in freestanding C.

At the hardware level, the NAND driver uses FMSS, a programmable microcontroller, to communicate with the NAND chips. lemonjesusâs earlier work on the S5L8702 sequencer, published as S5L8702-FMISS-Tools, documents its instruction set and provides tools for inspecting and building bytecode. That research is important prior work for understanding this part of the storage hardware; my work here uses the sequencer to read NAND as part of the nano 5G boot path.

Industry observers note that the loader first checks that the microsecond timer used for driver timeouts is running. It then initializes the read-only NAND and FTL stack, mounts the FAT filesystem, and opens /.rockbox/rockbox.ipod. The core sequence follows the Rockbox bootloaderâs own file-loading path:.

In a recent development, the file loader checks the Rockbox model identifier and checksum, then leaves the executable image at 0x08000000. The final handoff keeps interrupts masked, cleans and invalidates caches, drains pending writes, and branches to that address. Rockboxâs startup code takes over from there. If storage, mounting, or image loading fails, the payload indicates the failing stage on the LCD and stops.

On my nano 5G, the result is a cold, battery-powered boot straight into Rockbox, with no USB connection and no disk-mode button sequence. The PRVD partition setting skips rsrc validation and, when combined with the star exploit, enables untethered boot straight into Rockbox. The main constraint is that the font payload is limited to 27,874 bytes. Installation and restoration procedures, along with the reverse-engineering notes and build details, are in the nano5g_bootstub and nano5g_emCORE repositories below.

I have confirmed that the private-data partition works the same way on the nano 7G, which suggests the method will likely work on the 6G too. I initiative to get the nano 4G and 5G Rockbox ports into good shape before applying this method to the 6G and 7G.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a latest Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The enhancement also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

Industry observers note that second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a new “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

Australians will get the right to sue big tech under online safety deal

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (433 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • House of Representatives, Parliament House, Canberra.
  • It has been revealed that australians are set to win the right to sue tech companies over online harm, under a deal that clears the way for the country’s digital duty of care law.
  • In a recent development, the duty of care flips how Australia polices the internet: rather than regulators chasing harmful content after it spreads, platforms themselves must find and reduce foreseeable risks before people get hurt.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

House of Representatives, Parliament House, Canberra.

It has been revealed that australians are set to win the right to sue tech companies over online harm, under a deal that clears the way for the country’s digital duty of care law. Communications Minister Anika Wells declared the agreement with the Greens on Tuesday and noted the bill would pass parliament this week.

In a recent development, the duty of care flips how Australia polices the internet: rather than regulators chasing harmful content after it spreads, platforms themselves must find and reduce foreseeable risks before people get hurt. The bill passed the lower house in October, but needed Greens votes in the Senate after the opposition Coalition came out against it.

Australia moves to ban AI chatbots from ‘emotional intimacy’ with children.

Those votes came at a price, as individuals and groups of Australians will be able to sue platforms that breach their duty of care. A separate external complaints body will give people a faster route alongside the courts.

Industry observers note that the penalties grew in the bargain too. Companies that breach the duty now face fines of A$109mn (about €62mn) or up to 5% of global revenue. Wells said that figure sits between Canada’s 3% and the EU’s 6%, and noted courts in Europe tend to award a share of the maximum based on the case.

Recent findings suggest that the amended bill also names addictive design features, such as endless scroll and popularity meters, as a risk platforms must assess. It expands the eSafety regulator’s power to take down nudify apps and strengthens privacy protections.

Industry observers note that the definition of content that promotes hatred of women gets sharper too. Wells stated it is aimed at material pushing violence and harassment at children, not at opinions about feminism.

“If you build it, you should be responsible for its risks,” Wells told reporters in Canberra.

It has been revealed that the global-revenue penalty may not land well in Washington, which has objected to countries sizing fines on US tech companies by their worldwide earnings. Wells met the US ambassador, David Brat, on Tuesday morning and described the conversation as friendly, with differences still being worked through.

Once the law passes, platforms get a 12-month transition before the duty takes effect. It stacks on top of Australia’s under-16 social media ban, the world’s first, which has been in force since December.

  • Industry observers note that macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the tech giant’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time ….

Industry observers note that macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

Sources indicate that it’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.).

According to recent reports, I’m a big fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, users should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy owners at least would like a little more transparency and control.

According to recent reports, airPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant update in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, customers had to wait until it “just worked.”.

Apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an update, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

Make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

Another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

Recent findings suggest that will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

Once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech users may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that presently happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

Is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Axelera AI CEO Fabrizio Del Maffeo (left) and CTO Evangelos Eleftheriou.

Axelera AI, the Dutch organization building chips that run AI models, is in talks to raise $400M, Bloomberg reported today, and the capital would go towards developing its chips further.

The Eindhoven firm is also seeking hundreds of millions of dollars in EU grants, Bloomberg wrote, citing people familiar with the private talks. That capital would come through the bloc’s IPCEI scheme for strategic technology projects.

Sources indicate that the amount would be Axelera’s biggest yet, as the company closed a $250M round led by Innovation Industries in February, with BlackRock and Samsung’s venture arm among the backers. That took its total since 2021 past $450mn in equity, debt, and grants.

At the time, Axelera called it the largest investment ever made in a European AI chip organization. Another $400M would push the total towards $850M.

Axelera first made its name with its Metis chip, built to run AI on devices such as cameras, robots, and drones rather than in distant data centres. Running models at the edge cuts the power and bandwidth that cloud AI burns through, which is the tech giant’s core pitch.

Industry observers note that its newer products aim higher, as the Europa processor, introduced in September, targets generative AI and agentic workloads. The Titania chiplet, backed by an EU grant of up to €61.6M, goes after data centres and supercomputers.

It has been revealed that the business has scale to show too. Axelera mentioned in February it had shipped to its 500th customer, across defence, manufacturing, robotics, and security.

Industry observers note that brussels has reason to listen when the organization comes asking. Axelera pitches itself as the maker of Europe’s first fully homegrown AI acceleration platform. EU programmes already fund its scale-up as part of the push to cut reliance on foreign chips.

According to recent reports, when you need to create a new event, the Calendar app historically has required manually filling in various fields for the title, date, time, invitees, etc. By contrast, the excellent third-party app Fantastical lets you type in natural language and it automatically fills in relevant parameters based on what you type.

In iOS 27, Apple finally introduces its own natural language input for Calendar events. You can type out your event details and certain recognized parameters will be used to automatically fill in the detail fields.

While the feature still isn’t on par with what Fantastical offers, since it doesn’t support as many data points as the third-party alternative, it’s very much a step in the right direction.

In a recent development, apple has always pitched Siri as being like a personal assistant. As such, calendar-related tasks should have been Siri’s strong suit. But until iOS 27, you couldn’t actually manage your calendar very well using Siri.

According to recent reports, with Siri AI, that’s changed in a significant way. Now, you can do things like:.

One of my favorite personal examples is from this summer when the NFL schedule was released. I asked Siri to find the Dallas Cowboys schedule and add every game to my calendar, and it pulled this off with ease.

Siri is so much better than before at assisting with your calendar, and iOS 27.3 will bring even more capabilities soon.

Making a dumb TV just smart enough

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (657 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Qsantos

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that I own an old, cheap TV.
  • However, it is connected to my own desktop computer through an HDMI cable, so I can watch movies and TV series from the couch.
  • So, of course, I vowed never to get off the couch unnecessarily.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I own an old, cheap TV. It has no Internet connection, no fancy smart features that make you want to install a Pi-hole, and no ask-me-again-later updates.

However, it is connected to my own desktop computer through an HDMI cable, so I can watch movies and TV series from the couch. Setting it up used to involve going to my desk, enabling the secondary monitor, opening the relevant application, moving its window to the secondary monitor, setting it in fullscreen, going back to the couch, remembering I forgot my wireless keyboard, getting off the couch, grabbing my wireless keyboard, going back to the couch again, and then pressing the Space bar.

The most key quality of a programmer is laziness.

So, of course, I vowed never to get off the couch unnecessarily. And that meant controlling everything from the TV remote.

So, I got myself an IR transmitter and an IR receiver to tinker with:.

Then, I fished out an ESP32-C3 Mini devboard, a mini-breadboard, and a handful of jumper wires, and made the most basic device that could solve my woes:.

I have played around with Espressif MCUs before, including for early versions of the OmniMorse, but I must admit that Claude is just faster at it than I am. With the help of Opus 5.5, I identified the RC-5 IR codes for each remote button, and set up a few scripts so that a single button press on the remote would do the whole dance I described above.

But this first success unlocked much more.

I also own a bunch of old consoles. Getting everything hooked up is a chore, and makes a mess of wires. It would be much simpler to run an emulator on my computer and show it on the TV.

Thus, I installed DuckStation, PCSX2, Dolphin, Cemu and ES-DE, configured two Xbox controllers on each of them, and got Claude to start everything from a single button on the remote.

At this point, I was using two of the four colored buttons of the TV remote. So, of course, I had to come up with two more modes. I got Claude to add a Fireplace mode, which just plays 10-hour videos, the most vital one being a fireplace. And also Steam, in Big Picture mode.

Soon, there were regular issues with windows opening on the wrong screen, so I switched approaches. Instead of a large desktop on two screens, I resorted to multiseat, which I had always wanted to use, with two separate X sessions, one on each screen. This also allows using both screens at the same time without interference.

According to recent reports, but that did mean I could not directly control the windows on the TV from my regular session. So, again, I got Claude to make me an admin panel:.

Recent findings suggest that the virtual TV remote actually works, by sending directly through the device I cobbled together. The device also tracks volume being changed from the real remote, so things stay in sync. The rest is just commands to my computer, including a virtual gamepad, and a real-time stream of what is being displayed (mouse clicks work too!). Also, turning on an Xbox controller switches to the emulator or Steam mode, and turning the last one off goes back to the fireplace.

In a recent development, last, but not least, I took a significant amount of time making (telling Claude to make) everything fast. The whole thing took me about 10 hours in total, most of which was setting up console emulators.

Claude still needs to be kept on a tight leash: it sometimes wanted to go in the wrong direction, left obvious bugs, or suggested fixes that did not address the root cause. However, it saved me a bunch of time on the original problem, and lowered the effort enough to go above and beyond!

#165557. ChatGPT ads already drive over 1% of BestMoney owner’s finance conversions

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1103 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thenextweb ↗ Open Full Page

ChatGPT ads already drive over 1% of BestMoney owner’s finance conversions

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1103 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hila Gil-Dotan, chief marketing officer of Natural Intelligence.
  • Ads inside ChatGPT already drive more than 1% of the finance conversions at Natural Intelligence.
  • But a paid placement and an AI recommendation are two different things, she mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hila Gil-Dotan, chief marketing officer of Natural Intelligence.

Ads inside ChatGPT already drive more than 1% of the finance conversions at Natural Intelligence. The channel is only months old, its chief marketing officer, Hila Gil-Dotan, told TNW. The company runs the comparison sites BestMoney.com and Top10.com.

But a paid placement and an AI recommendation are two different things, she mentioned. Independent studies found the advertiser shows up in ChatGPT’s own answer only about 5% of the time, according to Gil-Dotan. It is usually that organic mention that shapes the decision, she said.

“Nobody reports on that part yet: there’s no impression, no click, and no shared data on how often a brand was recommended,” Gil-Dotan said.

In a recent development, natural Intelligence answered TNW’s questions on the AI-Era Attribution Blueprint, which the Interactive Advertising Bureau released on 12 November. It sorts every sale into one of three pathways: Human-Owned, AI-Assisted or AI-Executed. AI-influenced sales are sometimes reported as search or direct traffic, which can send the next marketing investment to the wrong channel, mentioned Caroline Giegerich, the IAB’s vice president for AI.

“The AI-Era Attribution Blueprint is honest about what the industry can’t yet substantiate,” IAB chief executive David Cohen stated in the launch announcement.

In a recent development, nobody in finance can give clean percentages for each pathway yet, and the IAB is right to say so, Gil-Dotan said. AI-Executed sales, where an agent completes the purchase, are close to zero in financial services. An agent cannot open a credit card or take out an insurance policy for someone, as regulation and identity checks keep a human in the loop.

In a recent development, renewals could be the first exception, she mentioned. A business loan could, in theory, roll over automatically. Later, an agent might re-shop someone’s cover after a move or a upcoming baby. Earlier this month, AI models failed Visa’s shopping benchmark for agents.

Industry observers note that AI-Assisted sales are the fast-growing middle, but they split in two and only one half is visible, she said. When someone clicks a BestMoney ad in ChatGPT and applies, the tech giant sees the click, the comparison and the partner’s confirmed sale. The other half is the organic answer.

From ChatGPT’s ad platform, Natural Intelligence gets impressions, clicks, spend and the conversions the platform reports. It connects those to its own data: what people compared, what they chose, and whether the partner confirmed the sale. That, Gil-Dotan noted, turns a click into evidence.

Even the paid side is only partly visible. On Google’s AI Max campaigns, advertisers cannot see how much traffic came from AI Overviews or AI Mode. Google reports all of it as top-of-page ads. People also see an ad, or click it, and come back weeks later, often through a branded search.

“That’s the old last-click problem in a upcoming place,” Gil-Dotan said.

Industry observers note that paid search sits at the bottom of the funnel, so the click and the sale line up. Social sits higher, so Meta never relied on clicks alone: it credits conversions after views and engagement, and offers lift tests. ChatGPT is heading the same way, she remarked, and now reports one-day view-through conversions next to click-throughs.

AI platforms, ChatGPT and Google alike, should tell advertisers what triggered an ad: the current conversation, or one from weeks ago. They should say whether the brand also appeared in the organic answer, and where, and which sources informed it. AI traffic also needs consistent labels, so it doesn’t vanish into “direct” or “search”, she said. The IAB’s blueprint also asks AI platforms to disclose whether recommendations are paid or organic and which sources informed them, and to label AI-originated traffic consistently.

Industry observers note that people also tell chatbots far more than they type into a search box. Search advertisers see the terms they appear for; AI has no equivalent yet. Anonymous, aggregated data could show an advertiser what the people seeing its ads care about most: price, reviews or a particular use. Platforms should never tie it to an individual user, she noted.

Sources indicate that natural Intelligence’s pitch called it the top financial advertiser on ChatGPT. OpenAI publishes no advertiser rankings, so the claim rests on independent trackers, Gil-Dotan mentioned. By their counts, BestMoney consistently ranks among the top finance advertisers. She cited SE Ranking, which counted BestMoney behind more than 13% of all ChatGPT ad units in its study. OtterlyAI found BestMoney advertising in 15 of the 16 industries it tracked, she said. US advertisers spent about $70m on ChatGPT ads in October.

It has been revealed that chatGPT visitors arrive at every stage. After its sites qualify them, their conversion rate on partners’ sites is in many cases very similar to search, she said. She warned against comparing the two on last click, as they often serve the same person at different moments. Natural Intelligence takes a multi-channel approach.

“ChatGPT is where people work out what they need, and search is where they go to act,” Gil-Dotan noted.

According to recent reports, the IAB’s own survey found 44% of ad buyers use branded search and direct traffic as stand-ins for AI influence they can’t track. That is directionally right but gives the credit to the wrong place, Gil-Dotan said. An AI conversation about life insurance often surfaces weeks later as a branded Google search. But branded search also catches TV, a friend’s tip and social campaigns. Only lift tests can separate AI’s effect from the rest.

Gil-Dotan pointed to Similarweb data in the blueprint, which indicates only 8.8% of AI-influenced visits arriving from the AI itself. Most came through search. Natural Intelligence also tracks how often, and in what tone, AI mentions brands in a category.

Sources indicate that her advice is to hold back paid AI placements in one region or for one period, then measure total sales rather than AI-labelled traffic. Brands can’t test organic answers that way. They should track how often AI mentions them for the questions that matter, and how it describes them.

“Start now, while AI ad inventory is still relatively uncrowded and cheap to test,” she mentioned.

It has been revealed that brands that build that baseline in 2027 will know what AI is actually worth to them, she mentioned. Nor should they measure AI on its own, as consumers move between ChatGPT, Google and Microsoft in a single decision.

Signal’s latest app revision on iPhone disables a key system feature: taking screenshots.

By default, owners who update and try to take a screenshot will see a message that says: “Screenshot prevented by ‘Block Siri AI’ setting.”.

Industry observers note that fortunately, there’s an easy workaround. Users who want to re-enable screenshots can do so by visiting Signal’s privacy settings and turning off the latest toggle that’s labeled ‘Block Siri AI.’.

Here’s exactly what that toggle does, per the in-app settings:.

Prevent Siri AI from scanning Signal content. This will also block you from taking screenshots in the app and App Switcher.

In a recent development, it’s good to see that users can manually disable the latest privacy setting if they want. But Signal’s decision to block screenshots does raise crucial questions about the potential gap in privacy tools for iOS developers.

Apple already lets you block Siri AI from accessing whichever apps you manually exclude, and that became even easier in iOS 27.2. But rather than directing customers to that system option, Signal seems to believe it needed to take action itself with this upgrade.

Sources indicate that in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar reveals how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. According to recent reports, in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar reveals how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session indicates how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also indicates how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

iOS 27 gives the Messages app a variety of welcome upgrades, including one I’ve found myself using a lot: a Smart Reply feature that’s now personalized to the user’s writing style.

When the first wave of Apple Intelligence features were announced in 2024, one that I immediately thought sounded useful was Smart Reply.

In a recent development, the idea behind Smart Reply is simple. Rather than needing to manually type out replies in Messages and Mail, your iPhone can offer prewritten replies you can choose and send with a couple taps.

Great in theory, but the ‘Smart’ part of Smart Reply struggled to materialize in iOS 18.

Fortunately, with a key Apple Intelligence upgrade in iOS 27, the newly introduced version of the feature finally lives up to its name. Per Apple:.

Smart Reply in Mail and Messages can now draw on a user’s personalized writing style.

Before, Smart Reply would look at the context of a conversation to craft its suggestions. But now, it also aims to match your writing style, punctuation, and tone.

In iOS 18, I almost never used Smart Reply. That’s because despite being fine at suggesting replies that technically worked, those suggestions didn’t sound like me at all.

That’s changed in iOS 27. Smart Reply now consistently impresses me. It no longer offers generic responses that sound like AI wrote them. Instead, its suggestions actually fit with my normal style of communication.

The only drawback is that right now, you’ll only ever see two Smart Reply suggestions. If Apple expanded the feature by letting you scroll horizontally through more options, I suspect I’d use Smart Reply even more.

Have you been using iOS 27’s Smart Reply feature in Messages? Let us know in the comments.

According to recent reports, orange Business’s fresh Protected Mode keeps companies’ AI work in France. It offers models from Mistral, LightOn, Alibaba’s Qwen, Google and OpenAI. Anthropic is not on that list: its models are offered only in the platform’s other setting, Open Mode, according to the line-ups an Orange Business spokesperson shared with TNW. Orange updates the line-up regularly, the spokesperson added.

Protected Mode is part of Live Intelligence, Orange Business’s generative and agentic AI platform for companies. With the mode on, the models, agents, data and documents stay in France. Orange runs that environment across its data centres and its Cloud Avenue platform. Orange Business launched it for all customers on 17 November at its OpenTech event in Paris.

“Businesses no longer want to choose between the power of artificial intelligence and the protection of their data,” said Anne-Marie Thiollet, chief product and marketing officer at Orange Business.

It has been revealed that protected Mode is not SecNumCloud-qualified at this stage, the spokesperson mentioned. SecNumCloud is the French cybersecurity agency ANSSI’s qualification for trusted cloud services. Two other Orange Business cloud offers do hold it: Cloud Avenue SecNum, in Grenoble data centres, and Cloud Avenue SecNum Dynamic, in Normandy. Both are infrastructure services for shared and dedicated environments.

Open Mode offers a wider choice of models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Mistral, hosted outside Orange in Europe or Switzerland. In both modes, Orange keeps no data and uses none of it to train models. It calls this Zero Data Retention.

In a recent development, companies choose which employees get each mode. Consumers with access to both can switch in one click, and their conversations and agents stay separate between the two.

Sources indicate that protected Mode is included in Live Intelligence Portal licences, with no separate charge for turning it on, the spokesperson noted. Customers pay for models, agents and MCP connectors in units in both modes. For similar models, the two modes use units at broadly the same rate. The overall cost depends on which models customers choose and how much they use them.

Live Intelligence launched commercially in November 2024. All of its more than 150 active customers are outside Orange, the spokesperson stated. They include public bodies such as public healthcare organisations and local authorities. Many are small and mid-sized companies. Its 140,000 people include Orange staff, and Orange does not give a breakdown. The number is changing fast as customers find fresh uses, the spokesperson said.

Sources indicate that rouen University Hospital is rolling the platform out across the Rouen Cœur de Seine Hospital Group. SICAP, an electricity distributor in the Loiret and Eure-et-Loir regions, uses it for day-to-day work.

“We were looking for a French solution that was easy to use and met very practical day-to-day needs,” said Guillaume Thielon, IT project manager at SICAP.

In March, Orange added Live Intelligence Studio, tools to build and run AI agents made with LangChain, the agent startup. It is also adding a service catalogue to help small and medium-sized businesses put AI to work. The launch came alongside Orange’s Wolof AI models and €250m for Orange Ventures.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home.
  • HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.
  • A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that indicates up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

In a recent development, “Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

In the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

In a recent development, it’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

It has been revealed that the Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

Lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

Industry observers note that the holiday shopping season is here, and Apple’s AirPods are sure to be one of the most popular gifts. If you’re shopping for AirPods, Apple sells three different models: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. Here’s how they compare.

AirPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

Here’s a full comparison between both AirPods 5 models:.

The key thing about AirPods 5 is their open-ear design, unlike the in-ear design of the AirPods Pro 3 (more on those later). Even with that open-ear design, AirPods 5 offer incredible Active Noise Cancellation capabilities.

If you are shopping for AirPods 5, I do recommend spending the extra $20 to get the higher-end model. The better charging case alone is worth the extra money. With Find My integration and a built-in speaker, you can track your AirPods and play a sound from the case if you lose them.

If the person you’re shopping for doesn’t like in-ear earbuds, AirPods 5 are an excellent choice.

For most people, though, AirPods Pro 3 are probably the better choice ….

In a recent development, airPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. With that in-ear design, AirPods Pro 3 can offer up to 3x stronger noise cancellation than AirPods 5. In my testing, this difference is notable.

AirPods Pro 3 also offer several other features you won’t find on AirPods 5, including a heart rate sensor for workouts, plus Hearing Test, Hearing Aid, and Hearing Protection features.

Sources indicate that I still think AirPods Pro 3 are one of the best products in Apple’s lineup today. I wear mine for multiple hours every single day and can’t imagine life without them. I love the in-ear fit, and the ANC still impresses me, whether I’m at home or somewhere like a coffee shop.

It has been revealed that if you know the person you’re shopping for (whether it’s yourself or someone else) likes the in-ear earbud design, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option. This is especially true when AirPods Pro 3 are on sale, like they are right now at $149. The price difference between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 is very small, and you’re getting a much better product.

Finally, we have AirPods Max. These are Apple’s only option for people who want AirPods in an over-ear headphone form factor. Last year, they were pretty hard to recommend since they’d gone five years without a real upgrade.

It has been revealed that this year, however, Apple officially introduced AirPods Max 2, bringing modern features to Apple’s high-end headphones. This includes features like Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Personalized Volume, and more.

It has been revealed that airPods Max 2 are a far more compelling option than AirPods Max were at this time last year. They’re still pricey, but I love the aesthetics and find them very comfortable. There’s something about the premium aluminum design with an elegant Digital Crown that really stands out.

In a recent development, if you’re looking to splurge this holiday season, AirPods Max 2 are a great choice. For more realistic budgets, I think AirPods Pro 3 are the best option.
